articles.title: Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
articles.summary:
Meta has tweaked its business terms to remove language suggesting that it could freely train its AI models on news sites, like The Verge — but legal experts say these changes aren’t enough to address their concerns. “This does nothing to restrict the ‘associated with your products or services’ [language] that would let Meta scrape entire sites,” James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell Law School, tells Nieman Lab.
Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
Meta’s new business terms could still help it justify training AI on scraped sites.
Initially, Meta’s new terms for business accounts appeared to give the company permission to train its AI on news sites. The terms, which go into effect October 30th, stated that Meta “may use any content” from the websites associated with a business account to “develop, research” and “train” Meta’s products. At the time, legal experts told Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta “to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions,” such as the robots.txt file that has historically told scrapers (including search engines like Google) what they are allowed to crawl.
Following fierce backlash from the publishing industry, Meta removed language saying it would “train” its products with scraped content. articles.title: Signal Vulnerability Lets Malicious Callers Block Hang-Ups
articles.summary:
Signal has resolved a critical-severity vulnerability that could allow a malicious caller to keep audio and video tracks enabled even after the user hung up.
The security defect is tracked as CVE-2026-113380 (CVSS score of 9.3) and impacts RingRTC, the open source library Signal uses for voice and video calls, which is based on WebRTC.
Due to the issue, a remote peer could flood the call’s Finite State Machine (FSM) event queue with junk, and the call would not terminate.
This happened because the hangup was not treated as a kill switch, but as an event added to the FSM event queue; there was no rate limit on peer-originated events; and the hangup event had no priority.
“Flood the queue with junk and the hang-up waits behind attacker noise forever, so the call (microphone, possibly camera) is never torn down,” a GitHub write-up by a researcher reads.
By exploiting the vulnerability, an attacker could keep the audio and video tracks flowing from a target device while the victim believes they ended the call.
The security defect was resolved in RingRTC version 2.72.0, which was released on September 4.
Details on the flaw, however, were published on Tuesday, along with a conceptual proof-of-concept (PoC). NIST added the CVE to the NVD database on Tuesday.
Signal resolved the issue by ensuring that call termination requests do not remain blocked in FSM’s event queue and are detected independently.

articles.title: L’heure d’hiver est de retour ce week-end : non, ce n'est toujours pas la dernière fois
articles.summary:
Plus que quelques jours avant le prochain changement d’heure. Nous vivons à l’heure d’été depuis la fin mars 2026, mais c’est bientôt terminé. La bascule aura lieu ce week-end, dans la nuit du samedi 24 au dimanche 25 octobre. La France passera alors à l’heure d’hiver.
Passage à l’heure d’hiver le 25 octobre 2026 : on dort plus ou moins ?
Comme à chaque changement d’heure, toute la question est de savoir dans quel sens s’effectue la bascule. Le site officiel de l’administration, Service public, donne la réponse : « Il faudra penser à reculer vos montres d’une heure dans la nuit du samedi 24 au dimanche 25 octobre 2026. » À 3 heures du matin, il sera donc 2 heures : la nuit de samedi à dimanche durera une heure de plus !
Faut-il pour autant se relever en pleine nuit pour régler toutes ses horloges ? Pas pour les smartphones, ordinateurs et tablettes : ils se mettent généralement à l’heure tout seuls, à condition que le réglage automatique de la date et de l’heure soit activé. En revanche, les montres classiques, les réveils, les horloges murales, les fours, les micro-ondes et les tableaux de bord des voitures non connectées devront encore être réglés à la main dimanche matin.
Ce changement d’heure peut donner l’impression qu’il intervient particulièrement tôt, et ce n’est pas totalement faux. Effectivement, l’an dernier nous sommes passés à l’heure d’hiver dans la nuit du 25 au 26 octobre.
Mais pourquoi change-t-on d’heure, au fait ?

The security research landscape is changing rapidly. AI has lowered the barrier to entry and become a genuine force multiplier. We use it across our own internal security programs, and we welcome researchers who do the same. articles.title: Localizing compliance at scale: Achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
articles.summary:
Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
For ten days, auditors appointed by the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) sat together with us and worked through 80 controls. That is what it took for a company headquartered in the United States, operating a global network serving Korean users, to be certified in South Korea. Cloudflare has now obtained South Korea's Information Security Management System (ISMS) certification under the ISMS-P framework.
For customers in Korea, this is more than a compliance checkbox. It is evidence that Cloudflare's security and privacy program has been examined not only for whether our controls exist, but for how they operate in the context of Korean law, the Korean language, and the particular expectations of Korean regulators.
What a Korean user sees when they sign up
The most visible result of this work is the Cloudflare account sign-up page. In most parts of the world, the line that sits above the sign-up button reads: "By continuing, I agree to Cloudflare's terms, privacy policy, and cookie policy."
A user signing up from South Korea sees something different. The Korean experience is triggered by the country selected at sign-up and by IP geolocation from within South Korea, and it breaks the same agreement into four separately labeled items, each marked required or optional, each linking to its full text, with an option to agree to all of them at once:

articles.title: Big Tech’s thirst for water is sparking a global resistance
articles.summary:
After ChatGPT was released in November 2022, the tech industry was quick to herald the chatbot as the marker of a new wave of technological progress. As companies pushed to create more powerful AI models, the water demand of their ambitions took a while to become clear. In April 2023, a research paper out of the University of California estimated that training the large language model behind the initial version of ChatGPT had required 185,000 gallons of water. For every extended conversation someone had with the chatbot or every time they asked it to write an email, they were effectively pouring a bottle of water down the drain.
That statistic got a lot of play when it was released. It became an early warning sign of what was coming as companies pushed chatbots as a universal technology that could replace psychologists, educators, lawyers, and even people’s friends or partners.
As public concern grew, Google and OpenAI came out with their own figures. The companies suggested that querying one of their chatbots used mere drops of water. Independent researchers were not impressed, arguing the companies were taking a narrow view of the water use necessary to power and cool increasingly monstrous data centers. Those water demands can be quite significant too.

“We’re starting with getting people from one place to the other, but we want to basically own transportation of any kind on Earth,” Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call Wednesday.
Tesla has previously shown a concept version of a multi-passenger vehicle it calls the “Robovan,” but it’s unclear if Taneja’s bombastic comments mean the company is working on other types of transportation.
What was clearer on the call is that Tesla’s Cybercab expansion will begin in Dallas next month and spread to other cities by the end of this year. Tesla already operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUV in small fleets in Dallas, Houston, and the Florida cities of Miami, Orlando, and Tampa. The company also said on its earnings call that it will start selling Cybercabs to fleet operators by the end of this year.
Broader expansion of the Cybercab could set up a real fight with Waymo, which is currently the market leader for robotaxis in the United States, with more than 4,000 of them deployed across more than a dozen cities. Tesla has argued that its Cybercab is cheaper and easier to build, which should allow it to undercut Waymo and other robotaxi operators on price. But the company has to reach real scale outside Austin in order to prove that point.

articles.title: Why Yango doesn't see Africa's fragmentation as a flaw
articles.summary:
Ask any founder who has built a business across different African markets, and they would agree the continent’s digital market is fragmented. The fragmentation shows up in how people pay, how businesses are regulated, consumer behaviour, and how digital services are delivered.
Companies also face different licencing requirements, tax regimes, data rules, infrastructure availability, and consumer behaviours as they move from one country to the next. Even within a single country, the rules can sometimes change from one city to another.
Norebase’s State of Expansion in Africa 2026 report offers a glimpse into just how different those markets can be. Based on data from more than 40,000 companies that have expanded through its platform, the report found differences in how long it takes to establish a business across African countries, as well as the rules and requirements companies have to navigate.
Yango Group, a Dubai-headquartered company that provides digital services, including mobility, delivery, foodtech, and entertainment across over 30 countries, has had to contend with many of those differences as it expands across African markets.
However, Adeniyi Adebayo, the company’s Chief Business Officer, sees the fragmentation differently. In an interview with TechCabal in October, he argued that while Africa is undoubtedly fragmented, the differences are more nuanced than they are often made out to be.

articles.title: Wenn Erdkruste und Erdmantel über den Erdkern gleiten: Warum die geografischen Pole um 10 Zentimeter pro Jahr wandern
articles.summary:
Zehn Zentimeter pro Jahr: Warum die geografischen Pole der Erde wandern
Die geografischen Pole der Erde verschieben sich derzeit mit einer per Satellit gemessenen Geschwindigkeit von rund zehn Zentimetern pro Jahr, was die durchschnittliche Driftgeschwindigkeit tektonischer Platten übersteigt. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, handelt es sich bei solchen Geschwindigkeiten nicht bloß um kurzlebige Ausreißer der Gegenwart, da vergleichbare Verschiebungen in den vergangenen 320 Millionen Jahren mehrfach über Zeiträume von jeweils zehn Millionen Jahren auftraten.
Ein Forschungsteam um den Geowissenschaftler Mathew Domeier, den Geologen Leandro C. Gallo, die Geowissenschaftlerin Chloé M. Marcilly und den Geophysiker Trond H. Torsvik von der norwegischen Universität Oslo wies insgesamt vier solcher Phasen anhand urzeitlicher Meeresspiegelschwankungen nach. Diese Episoden lagen in den Zeitfenstern vor 200 bis 190 Millionen, vor 150 bis 140 Millionen, vor 100 bis 90 Millionen sowie vor 30 bis 20 Millionen Jahren und erreichten Raten von mindestens 0,6 Breitengraden pro einer Million Jahre, was mindestens 6,7 Zentimetern pro Jahr entspricht.

articles.title: Running Frontier-Class AI Models Across 8 NVIDIA DGX Spark Nodes | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
AI developers aren’t just running a single model anymore—they’re orchestrating multiple models in parallel, chaining inference calls, and experimenting with frontier-class architectures that demand hundreds of gigabytes of memory. NVIDIA DGX Spark was built to bring AI development to the desk, and now you’ll be able to link even more Spark nodes together.
At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA announced official support for eight-node DGX Spark clusters, scaling unified memory to 1 TB and opening the door to frontier-class models, multi-agent workloads, and near-linear pre-training—all running locally.
NVIDIA Sync makes it easy to cluster. Its Cluster Assistant handles setup and device management. Support for eight-node clusters in NVIDIA Sync is coming by the end of the year.
Read on for benchmark data on how inference, orchestration, and training scale as the cluster grows.
Run larger, newer frontier-class models
The biggest benefit of an eight-node cluster is memory. A single DGX Spark provides 128 GB of unified memory; four nodes reach 512 GB; eight nodes reach 1 TB. That capacity opens the door to a class of models that previously wouldn’t start on a four-node system, including the full GLM 5.3 (753B) model from Z.ai.

articles.title: « Cette fois, je ne le ferai pas » : Trump voulait rebaptiser l’océan Atlantique, Google dit non

Mais cette fois-ci, Sundar Pichai ne semble pas vouloir « lécher le cul » de Donald Trump.
Le changement de trop
Lors d’un meeting organisé en Caroline du Sud, Donald Trump a raconté à ses supporters un échange qu’il aurait eu avec le patron de Google. Fier de ses précédentes « conquêtes » cartographiques, Trump a déclaré avoir contacté Google, pour demander à Sundar Pichai de « gérer » le changement de nom de l’océan Atlantique. Un changement qui ne passe pas. « Non, non, non. Cette fois, je ne le ferai pas », aurait répondu Pichai, avant d’expliquer que les océans étaient différents, puisqu’ils bordent « de nombreux pays ». Des implications internationales qui suffiraient à ralentir Google.
Pour justifier les précédents changements locaux, Google indiquait s’appuyer sur les dénominations officielles du Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), la base de données américaine des noms géographiques. Or, celle-ci conserve pour l’instant le nom d’« océan Atlantique ». Reste à savoir si Google suivrait le mouvement si le nom venait à changer officiellement. Contacté par le Washington Post, le groupe n’a pas confirmé que l’appel rapporté par Donald Trump avait bien eu lieu.

articles.title: Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction
articles.summary:
Weather forecasts shape more than daily plans; timely weather information is crucial for energy producers, insurers and transport operators to plan around changing conditions. A global forecast can show a storm taking shape, but decisions about solar farms, shipping routes or insured property depend on what happens locally.
NVIDIA Earth-2 gives developers and researchers a family of open AI models and tools they can customize with their own data. Running on NVIDIA computing, these technologies support global weather prediction, detailed regional forecasts and environmental research.
StormScope EU is the latest model to join Earth-2 — a regional version of the StormScope model for short-term forecasting, trained over Europe weather and climate data. It uses EUMETSAT satellite observations to predict evolving cloud conditions across 16 Meteosat channels at 10-minute intervals.
At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing a live StormScope EU pipeline in an interactive weather demo built in partnership with Earthmover. The demo uses Earth2Studio to run forecasts and Earthmover’s data platform to manage and serve the real-time results, which are updated as soon as new satellite observations come in, every 10 minutes. Earthmover serves these results as map tiles, letting visitors explore predictions across Europe without downloading entire datasets.

articles.title: Quest Diagnostics sufrió un ciberataque que expuso historiales médicos de sus pacientes en Estados Unidos
articles.summary:
Quest Diagnostics, la mayor red de laboratorios clínicos de Estados Unidos, informó que sufrió un ciberataque con acceso no autorizado a historiales médicos de sus pacientes, según reveló la propia empresa ante el regulador bursátil del país.
La compañía, que según su propio sitio institucional atiende a uno de cada tres adultos estadounidenses y a la mitad de los médicos y hospitales del país cada año, detectó la intrusión el miércoles y notificó a las autoridades federales al día siguiente.
El dato quedó asentado en una presentación ante la Comisión de Bolsa y Valores de Estados Unidos (SEC, el organismo que regula los mercados financieros del país), a la que accedieron varios medios estadounidenses.
El acceso indebido afectó al Quanum Lab Services Manager, la plataforma que algunos médicos y centros de salud usan para solicitar análisis de laboratorio en nombre de sus pacientes y consultar los resultados una vez procesados. La empresa dijo que un atacante no identificado habría visto “ciertos historiales de pacientes”, aunque el alcance exacto todavía está bajo investigación.
Quest Diagnostics remarcó que, hasta el momento, el incidente no alteró de forma significativa sus operaciones comerciales y que ya trabaja junto a una firma externa de ciberseguridad para contener el ataque y determinar con precisión qué información quedó expuesta y a cuántas personas afectó.

Its SafeGuard AI platform is designed to analyze data from distributed control systems, safety instrumented systems, process historians, alarm management systems and IT security tools. The company says it uses that information to identify anomalies and changes to engineering configurations, protection settings and safety functions that may need operator attention.
The approach targets a gap Indurex sees in conventional OT security tools, which often focus on network-connected assets and activity. articles.title: Astronomische Spurensuche: Was fünf Sterne im Zentrum über Van Goghs „Sternennacht“ verraten
articles.summary:
Astronomische Spurensuche: Was die 5 Sterne im Zentrum über van Goghs „Sternennacht“ verraten
Schon in den 1980er-Jahren suchten zwei Forscher am Himmel nach Vorbildern für van Goghs Sternennacht: Albert Boime 1984 und Charles Whitney 1986. Doch ihre Ergebnisse widersprachen sich und führten zu keinem stichfesten Beweis. Ihre astronomischen Erklärungsversuche setzten sich daher nicht gegen die verbreitete Deutung durch, das Bild sei vor allem religiös oder symbolisch zu verstehen. Ein Brief an van Goghs Bruder Theo hatte das Bild bislang mit der Zeit um den 18. Juni 1889 in Verbindung gebracht.
Nach Angaben des koreanischen Forschungsteams hat seither niemand mehr untersucht, ob die Anordnung der gemalten Sterne nicht doch zu einem Himmel passt, den der Künstler tatsächlich vor Augen hatte. Die Ergebnisse wurden in Scientific Reports, einer Zeitschrift des Nature-Portfolios, veröffentlicht.
Nicht das Sternbild Widder, sondern Stier
Als der Astronom Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim frühere Deutungen von Vincent van Goghs „Sternennacht“ las, stutzte er: Andere Forschende hatten die Sterne im Bild dem Sternbild Widder zugeordnet. Kim und sein Team erkannten darin stattdessen den Sternhaufen der Hyaden im Stier. „Da das Team bereits viele Teleskope gebaut und jahrelang den Nachthimmel beobachtet hatte, hielt es das Sternbild Widder für eine unwahrscheinliche Inspirationsquelle des Malers“, heißt es in einer Pressemitteilung.

articles.title: How to Read Data into GPU Memory in Python with NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
GPU applications are processing ever-growing datasets with increasingly powerful accelerators. According to the 2025 Stanford AI Index, compute for notable AI models has been doubling approximately every five months, while the size of datasets used to train LLMs has been doubling approximately every eight months. As computation and data scale together, moving data efficiently from storage becomes a necessity for keeping accelerators supplied.
NVIDIA Magnum IO GPUDirect Storage (GDS) addresses this challenge by enabling a direct data path between supported storage and GPU memory. This avoids unnecessary staging through CPU memory and reduces overall CPU utilization in the system. GDS is supported by a growing ecosystem that includes many major storage vendors.
At the application layer, Python plays a central role in modern AI development. As of August 2025, nearly half of all new AI projects on GitHub were built primarily in Python while the main application interface to GDS is the cuFile C API.
NVIDIA KvikIO, a Python and C++ library for high-performance file I/O, bridges this gap. It provides high-level, idiomatic Python and C++ interfaces, along with additional controls over how I/O requests are performed.
The tutorial in this post demonstrates how to use the NVIDIA KvikIO Python API to configure storage I/O, read data into GPU memory, and confirm that the accelerated path within GDS was activated. It also shows how to inspect the KvikIO and cuFile settings that influence t…

articles.title: PC shipments dropped over 20 percent in Q3 due to RAM price hikes
articles.summary:
Demand for new PCs took a hit after months of price hikes, with Counterpoint Research reporting global PC shipments fell 21 percent year-over-year in Q3 2026. That’s in line with earlier reports from IDC and Omdia. It’s not just PCs, either — that same quarter, smartphone shipments also hit a 14-year low.
PC shipments dropped over 20 percent in Q3 due to RAM price hikes
Counterpoint Research says higher prices are tanking demand for new PCs.
Counterpoint linked the decline in PC shipments to higher component prices. Up until Q2 2026, PC shipments had been growing for over two years straight. But over the last several months, RAM, SSDs, and chips from Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm have all gotten more expensive, leading to price hikes on everything from MacBooks to Raspberry Pis. Counterpoint senior analyst Minsoo Kang noted that some companies are shifting to “prioritize configurations that can better absorb component inflation,” leaving fewer affordable options for price-sensitive buyers. Some companies are even reviving older tech, like DDR4 RAM and 4GB GPUs, to help mitigate price hikes.
Counterpoint also says Q3 2025 included “purchases ahead of the Windows 10 support deadline and tariff-related inventory adjustments,” which added to the sharp year-over-year drop this past quarter. articles.title: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
articles.summary:
Sponsored
Provided byWD
Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs.
What happens to data after a model responds? Much of the back-end data that’s generated—from billions of daily prompts, images, and videos—needs to be stored. But data storage is one of the harder infrastructure costs to plan for, and it’s often overlooked in initial AI infrastructure planning.
As inference scales, the data footprint grows with it
Traditionally, AI infrastructure conversations have centered on the compute-intensive process of training a model. Training is finite: a run starts, burns through compute, and ends. But inference runs continuously, every time a model answers a prompt. For infrastructure planning, that difference matters: A training run is a project you can budget for and retire. Inference doesn’t retire; every inference request leaves something behind.
Take AI-generated video. In this workload, the back-end spend can be significant. From internal measurements, WD found that an 8-second clip (returned to a user as a 3.97MB 720p file) left more than 500MB of associated data behind on the back end, including logs, cached context, immediate renders, backups, and safety records. That’s a 130x increase over the output file size the user saw. Scale this to an enterprise generating longer, higher resolution video and the back-end …

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: Hacker Conversations: Corey Thuen and the Evil Bit
articles.summary:
Corey Thuen is a hacker with a hacker mindset that is focused on the right way to do wrong things to get the right result.
Corey Thuen is the founder and CEO of Gravwell, a firm with a slight difference: it develops data analytics and vulnerability detection through a combined team of big data experts and hackers.
When interviewing a candidate for the hacker half of the team, he looks for people who have what he calls ‘the evil bit’. “Do they have that ‘evil streak’? Do they have that adversarial mindset that can look at a product and seek out ways to exploit it? If they don’t have that evil bit, I don’t think we can teach it.” He accepts that it may be possible for some people to develop one, but in his own experience, it’s either there or it’s not. Natural-born hacker is more a fact than a description; and it is tempting to describe Thuen as a natural-born hacker himself.
But does ‘evil’ indicate a lack of morality? “Who defines morality?” he replied. “Who defines what is good and what is bad? The old school hacking ethos, which still lingers, is that all information should be free”. Other folks consider that a bad viewpoint.
“I was recently working for the US government. We were evaluating the systems that go into power substations, part of the critical infrastructure. So, we were hacking these systems, but the goal was to improve security for everyone. We were using the evil streak for good. Hacking skills are a bit like guns. Neither are evil in themselves. Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them

Canva Craft can generate images at up to 2K resolution and in more than 30 aspect ratios. In addition to generating social media posts and marketing content, it’s also supposed to create realistic scenes, digital art, environmental imagery, and more. articles.title: ChatGPT e outras IAs mudam resultados de testes de personalidade conforme o idioma
articles.summary:
Pesquisadores da Universidade de Ciência e Tecnologia da China propuseram testes de personalidade para cinco diferentes chatbots. Cada inteligência artificial respondeu aos testes em pelo menos dois idiomas diferentes, à medida que a língua mudava, mudavam também o conteúdo social das respostas, como negatividade, curiosidade e “cultura”.
Foram utilizados para o estudo o ChatGPT-4o, o Gemini 2.0 Flash, o DeepSeek-V3, o Ernie 3.5 e o Le Chat, com cada um deles respondendo perguntas em inglês e mandarim. O LeChat, IA francesa, também respondeu em seu idioma nativo. Os resultados foram publicados na revista Royal Society Open Science no mês passado.
Para quem tem pressa:
- Pesquisadores da Universidade de Ciência e Tecnologia da China avaliaram cinco chatbots com um teste de personalidade em inglês e mandarim. O Le Chat também respondeu em francês;
- Os resultados mostraram que as respostas variavam conforme o idioma. O ChatGPT-4o, por exemplo, teve pontuação de abertura mental de 4,74 em inglês e 4,03 em mandarim. Já o DeepSeek-V3 apresentou o resultado inverso;
- Ao comparar as respostas das IAs com dados de testes feitos por pessoas, os pesquisadores encontraram diferenças culturais significativas. O estudo indica que o idioma pode influenciar os traços de personalidade demonstrados pelos chatbots

articles.title: Telstra to enable RCS to enrich messaging between iPhone and Android users - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Telstra has announced it will be enabling Rich Communication Services (RCS) from next month to allow a better messaging experience between Android smartphones and iPhones.
This comes almost 3 years after Apple officially decided to adopt RCS to improve texting between iPhone and Android with higher quality and security.
The difference between iPhone and Android messaging has been clearly obvious without RCS with blue and green bubbles in the message thread.
The blue bubbles indicate it came from an iPhone or was part of iMessage and green showing the message came from an Android device.
RCS not only provides greater security but also other features like read receipts and indications when the other person is typing their reply.
Will also allow sharing of images and videos in their full quality. Pre-RCS communication between iPhone and Android users meant attachments were severely compressed.
Until now these messaging features were only available for iPhone-to-iPhone and Android-to-Android messaging.
RCS will finally fill the great divide between iPhone and Android messaging.
Telstra to roll out RCS for Android customers from November 16, with iOS customers able to use RCS after the December iOS release.
Telstra’s RCS rollout is scheduled for completion by the end of 2026.
No word on when Optus and Vodafone will run their own respective RCS rollouts.

articles.title: Flutterwave offers employees share-backed loans in rare move
articles.summary:
Flutterwave employees can now borrow money against their vested shares without selling them, through a programme with Techdollar, a US private-credit startup. The loans give staff access to cash before a company sale or stock-market listing while allowing them to retain any future gains on their equity.
“I always say that our people are our secret sauce and the driving force behind our success at Flutterwave, and we believe they should share in the value they create without having to wait for a major liquidity event,” Olugbenga “GB” Agboola, Flutterwave’s founder and CEO, said in a statement.
The deal offers an alternative to selling shares during a funding round or waiting years for an exit—two of the few ways startup employees in Africa have historically been able to turn equity into cash. Flutterwave, valued at $3.25 billion, said in April that it was not close to an initial public offering (IPO).
Techdollar will lend against employees’ vested shares for six to 12 months, typically advancing less than half their value. If a borrower defaults, the lender can seize and sell the pledged shares. Employees keep their equity if they repay the loan but risk losing it if they don’t.
The loans will be paid into accounts that employees open with Nuvion, a Miami-based digital bank for businesses that already powers Flutterwave’s stablecoin products.

articles.title: Developer Behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready
articles.summary:
Brandon Thomas put his AI-built open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications in front of Hacker News and immediately deflated them. "I wasn’t ready to post this to HN," he wrote. "It’s not anywhere close to read" He said he would post again once the project clears beta.
Announcement posts had gone up across five subreddits days earlier carrying a different message, projecting beta and roughly 100% parity within a month. The repository sides with the Hacker News version.
Thomas used Claude Opus 5.5 to build the applications in Rust, with WebAssembly builds for the browser, mirroring Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign and Acrobat Pro. All of it ships under MIT and Apache licenses.
PhotoCraft’s ROADMAP.md, updated October 11, puts feature breadth at roughly 76%, from counts: 628 of 628 menus, 56 of 68 tools, 30 of 35 panels, 13 plus 4 of 31 formats. Then comes a second number. Readiness for real work is about 45%. A mainstream practitioner gets 43%; someone using core features only gets 61%. Beta is 1,100 to 1,800 hours out and full parity 2,300 to 4,100, counted as Opus 5.5 agent wall-clock hours for one agent working sequentially. The target is named exactly: Photoshop 2026, version 27.11.0, measured from the installed application on October 10.

articles.title: Weltraumteleskop Euclid entdeckt ganz nebenbei einen unbekannten Kometen
articles.summary:
Per Zufall: Weltraumteleskop Euclid entdeckt unbekannten Kometen
Euclids eigentliche Aufgabe ist ambitioniert: Das Weltraumteleskop der Europäischen Raumfahrtbehörde ESA soll eine dreidimensionale Karte des Universums erstellen. Die Daten sollen auch dabei helfen, Dunkle Materie und Dunkle Energie besser zu verstehen.
Seit dem Missionsstart des Teleskops im Juli 2023 hat Euclid bereits beeindruckende Aufnahmen geliefert. Erst im Juni 2026 veröffentlichte die ESA etwa eine Aufnahme des Zentrums der Milchstraße, auf der mehr als 60 Millionen Sterne zu sehen sind.

articles.title: Can AI make debt collections less about chasing and more about predicting?
articles.summary:
Can AI make debt collections less about chasing and more about predicting?
The future lies in using data to understand portfolios, AI to prioritise decisions, and human judgement where individual circumstances matter most.
Defaults are inevitable.
For the past few years, we have been hearing about predictive analytics that can identify a borrower who is going to default before the default actually happens.
Time and again, we have seen the limits of this idea.
Defaults aren't a prediction problem that technology will eventually eliminate. Defaults are an uncertainty that lending produces, by design. What lenders need is not machinery that assumes this uncertainty can be removed, but machinery designed to operate effectively under it.
You cannot predict at an individual borrower level who is going to default. You can, at best, predict, over a sufficiently large cohort of borrowers, what the default rate might be.
The behaviour of large groups can be predicted statistically. The behaviour of a particular individual cannot.
If you have one million borrowers, you can make remarkably good statements about what will happen to the portfolio. Narrow it to 100,000 borrowers in Karnataka, and you can still make useful predictions. Narrow it further by repayment history, geography, employment, credit score and other risk characteristics, and you can create increasingly meaningful cohorts.
But as the cohorts get smaller, the certainty of those predictions starts decreasing.

A primer on this crucial and frankly mysterious piece of climate science.
How much do you know about permafrost?
Maybe, like me, you’ve been aware that this layer of frozen soil is thawing, that it’s important in the global puzzle of climate change … and that’s about the extent of it.
The great news for both of us is that my colleague James Temple just published two in-depth stories about permafrost. His reporting took him to the boreal forests of Alaska, where he helicoptered into the wilderness to learn more about how this material could affect our climate both now and in the future.
I’d recommend you give both of James’s stories a read. There’s this feature about efforts to tackle the intensifying fires that are threatening permafrost, as well as this look at how researchers are trying to understand the complicated tangle of potential climate effects. Permafrost is a massive blind spot for climate change
Permafrost is the frozen layer of soil that’s under about 15% of land around the Northern Hemisphere. While technically material needs to be frozen for only two consecutive years to count as permafrost, most of our current permafrost formed during the last ice age.

Google turns the infrastructure behind Gemini’s agents into a cloud service
Google will soon make the infrastructure that powers its Gemini agents available to Google Cloud users in preview.
Announced on Thursday at the Linux Foundation’s AGNTCon+MCPCon in San Jose, Agent Compute Engine will become available in preview to Google Cloud users later this year. It will provide every AI agent with a hardware-isolated microVM that combines the speed of containers with the security of a sandbox.
Who else offers agent sandboxes?
The idea of agent sandboxes is anything but new, of course. Startups like E2B and Daytona offer them to developers (and support them on any cloud), as does AWS with Bedrock AgentCore.
E2B runs each sandbox in a Firecracker microVM, the open source virtualization technology AWS originally built for Lambda. It can pause a sandbox with its memory and filesystem intact and resume it in about a second. Daytona started out with containers but added microVM sandboxes in July. Those can pause a full machine or fork a running one into identical copies.
AgentCore also gives every agent session its own microVM. AWS doesn’t charge for CPU while an agent waits on a model or tool call, though memory keeps billing until the runtime reclaims it. Those sessions top out at eight hours. In August, AWS added EC2-based runtime instances that can keep shared sessions alive for up to 14 days.

articles.summary:
The bad week for cybersecurity just got worse for thousands more companies, who were spied on by Chinese hackers following the breach of IT management and remote access giant ConnectWise.
Security researchers at Microsoft say the China state-aligned hackers broke into ConnectWise’s cloud backup service and stole application credentials that are used to establish data links between ConnectWise and its corporate customers, who rely on the cloud service to back up their company’s data.
By stealing the credentials, the hackers could log in to the customer’s Microsoft-hosted environment as if they were an authorized user and access their emails and other files.
According to Microsoft, the hackers used AI agents to rapidly hack into around 2,250 organizations at a rate of almost 3,000 attempted sign-ins per minute. Microsoft said this speed gives defenders “little time to detect and respond.”
The speed of the mass-hacks was attributed to the use of AI agents, specifically ARTEX, an open source AI framework that works with AI models to stress-test cyber defenses. The same AI software was used in a recent compromise of South Korea’s financial systems, many of which had weak security and lacked multi-factor authentication.
ConnectWise said it’s paused access to its cloud backup system and is investigating the breach. As of Thursday, the company said it was working on restoring the service.

The emails claimed to be from credit card companies and sent unsuspecting recipients to fake websites in an attempt to capture their credit card information. It's believed that the computer was administered remotely, allowing it to remain in situ without any in-person maintenance required.

articles.title: A era dos agentes de IA está mudando a Engenharia de Software. E isso é uma boa notícia para desenvolvedores
articles.summary:
Por: Maurício Aniche, CTO e cofundador da Alura
Por muito tempo, a produtividade em software esteve associada à capacidade de escrever código mais rápido.
Novas linguagens, frameworks, bibliotecas e plataformas surgiam com a promessa de reduzir o esforço necessário para transformar uma ideia em um produto digital. Em certa medida, era isso mesmo: a história da tecnologia pode ser contada como uma sucessão de ferramentas que diminuíram o custo de implementação.
A inteligência artificial generativa, e mais recentemente a inteligência artificial agêntica, é mais um capítulo dessa história. Mas talvez seja o capítulo que mais acelerou essa transformação.
Hoje, ferramentas baseadas em IA conseguem gerar funções, criar testes, sugerir arquiteturas e até executar tarefas relativamente complexas em poucos minutos. Com a chegada dos agentes de IA, começamos a ver sistemas capazes de atuar em diferentes etapas do ciclo de desenvolvimento, analisando código, propondo mudanças, executando validações e colaborando com equipes técnicas de maneiras que seriam difíceis de imaginar poucos anos atrás.
Diante desse cenário, uma pergunta se tornou recorrente: se a IA consegue programar, ainda faz sentido aprender engenharia de software?
A resposta é sim. E, paradoxalmente, talvez a engenharia de software nunca tenha sido tão importante.
O motivo é simples: software nunca foi apenas código.

articles.title: This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display
articles.summary:
Last year, we reported on Red Viper, a Virtual Boy emulator that added a splash of Super Game Boy-style color to Nintendo’s famously failed red-on-black “portable” 3D headset from the ’90s. Now, a new emulation experiment, VBoy Color, has taken the concept to a higher level, using a tile-based palette system that allows for many more distinct colors in each individual Virtual Boy frame.
Rather than simply replacing the Virtual Boy’s four shades of red with four different colors, VBoy Color’s readme files explain how the emulator’s game-specific Color Packs can assign a distinct four-color palette to each 8×8 tile in a Virtual Boy scene. That means the emulator can differentiate between green pipes, grey platforms, and red brick wall in Mario Clash, for instance, even though all those in-game objects share the same overlapping red hues in the original game.
The Game Boy Color-esque results feel like being transported into an alternate history where Nintendo invested in a full-color display rather than cheaper red LEDs for the Virtual Boy hardware. The increased contrast between differently colored elements is particularly welcome in games like Jack Bros. or Vertical Force, where the original red-on-red display often makes it hard to differentiate the player-character from busy red background elements.

- Date:

- Source:

Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

Prince of Persia, a threat group sponsored by the Iranian government, ran one of its command-and-control (C&C) servers from the United States this year, after a months-long lull in its operations, according to Semperis.
The APT actor, also tracked as Infy, has been operating for close to 20 years. Its targets are mostly Iranian dissidents, along with government and private entities in the US, Europe, and the Middle East.
Tomer Bar, AVP of security research at Semperis, tracked the group in his previous role at SafeBreach. He says that within a week of SafeBreach’s February 2026 report, the hackers took a C&C server offline and later relocated the rest of their servers.
Prince of Persia then halted operations for three months, a longer silence than any other in its nearly two-decade history. The pause overlapped with the war between Iran and the US and Israel, which broke out on February 28.
Semperis told SecurityWeek that this is the longest downtime it has confirmed, as its researchers were monitoring the group’s infrastructure the entire time. Earlier quiet periods reflected gaps in researchers’ visibility into the group’s operations rather than confirmed inactivity.
Prince of Persia’s operations restarted on May 27 with the deployment of a new C&C server, and data theft resumed. Within seven days, Tonnerre, one of the group’s malware families, had siphoned over 1,800 files from a single victim.

articles.title: AI agent security is a lifecycle — not a gatekeeper
articles.summary:
AI agent security is a lifecycle — not a gatekeeper
Enterprise security has traditionally operated on a relatively straightforward premise: establish identity, authenticate the requester, determine what that identity can access, and enforce those permissions.
AI agents introduce a fundamental complication. They don’t simply access systems. They interpret objectives, select tools, create sub-agents, make decisions, and execute actions, often using credentials and permissions inherited from humans.
The problem isn’t necessarily that an agent lacks proper credentials. It’s that those credentials may authorize actions the human never intended the agent to perform. And unlike conventional software, agents can change their execution paths dynamically in pursuit of an objective.
“The problem isn’t necessarily that an agent lacks proper credentials. It’s that those credentials may authorize actions the human never intended the agent to perform.”
This creates a new operational requirement: security must evaluate not only who or what is acting, but what an agent is attempting to do, on whose authority, and under which policy. Meeting that requirement takes more than a security checkpoint. It requires a continuous agent security lifecycle.
Defense-in-depth needs action-level authorization
Every passing day further shows that agent security is a defense-in-depth problem. Network security controls how agents communicate. Endpoint and runtime protections constrain where and how code execut…

articles.title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
articles.summary:
Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance. The same tasks run locally or in Docker Cloud Sandboxes, and Docker says it has tested Harbor with 64 concurrent tasks in the cloud.
Evaluating a coding agent means letting it install packages, edit files, and run commands, and a benchmark repeats this thousands of times. Docker's engineers describe this as running untrusted, AI-written code at scale. They also flag reward hacking, where an agent earns a passing score by tampering with tests or overwriting the file that records its score instead of solving the task. Harbor manages orchestration. It runs tasks, collects scores, and logs. It also supports benchmarks like Terminal-Bench. It needs an execution environment that is both isolated and consistent.
Each task runs in a Docker Sandbox, a microVM with its own kernel, so agent activity stays inside the VM and cannot reach the host, other tasks, or anything outside the environment. In Docker Cloud Sandboxes, configurable network policies let a task pull dependencies during setup, then restrict internet access while the agent works. Every agent is then evaluated under the same network conditions, which addresses a common source of non-reproducible results. Docker Compose is supported, so Harbor can run multi-container tasks in…

articles.title: Africa's stablecoin promise and the off-ramp problem
articles.summary:
On paper, it was a revolution. Over the past three years, three of Africa’s largest multi-licensed payment service providers each independently piloted a stablecoin rail. Between them, they process cross-border payments for merchants, e-commerce platforms, and remittance companies, as well as trade settlements, totalling billions of dollars annually. Their models promised to cut the cost of cross-border money movement by 10x. After stress-testing the off-ramp, each settled on a mix of stablecoin and traditional bank rails.
The blockchain worked, but the off-ramp did not. Converting back into local currency costs more than 8%, and in thin markets, the savings disappear.
Their experience exposes a truth the industry keeps skipping: stablecoins will not fix African cross-border finance until founders fix local liquidity.
I sit on a venture fund’s investment committee and back startups as an angel investor. Every cross-border fintech and payments startup that pitches me today is a stablecoin startup. Stablecoins are now table stakes for anyone building across borders. The case is not imaginary. Sub-Saharan Africa remains the most expensive region to send money to, averaging 8.5% on a $200 transfer compared with 6% globally, according to the World Bank. Chainalysis estimates that a $200 remittance sent from the region costs about 60% less when using stablecoins.

Shiprocket’s fastrr taps food commerce with new restaurant partnerships
Shiprocket’s fastrr has partnered with Punjabi Angithi operator Vegorama Group and Bikkgane Biryani to expand into food commerce, helping the brands manage direct orders, customer engagement and hyperlocal deliveries.
Shiprocket’s AI-native commerce platform, fastrr, has entered the food commerce segment through partnerships with Vegorama Group, which operates Punjabi Angithi, and Bikkgane Biryani.
The partnerships come as restaurant brands explore ways to drive orders through their own digital channels rather than relying solely on third-party food aggregators. Direct channels can also give restaurants greater access to customer data and more opportunities to engage with diners after a purchase.

articles.title: What Breaks When Packaging Moves From Wafer To Panel?
articles.summary:
Engineers are discovering many things they thought were process assumptions were actually wafer assumptions.
Key Takeaways:
Moving advanced packaging from wafer to panel sounds, at first, like a geometry problem. Large AI and HPC packages are increasingly rectangular, while the 300mm wafer underneath them is still round. As the package size grows, more of that expensive processing ends up around the circle’s edges where nothing useful can be built.
A panel gives that area back. It can fit more large packages into the same process cycle, and unlike a wafer, its dimensions don’t impose the same hard limit on the size of a square or rectangular package. For advanced packages that keep getting larger, the economics are difficult to ignore.
But the semiconductor packaging sector has spent decades learning how to process wafers, not panels. Equipment, materials, recipes, handling systems, and process controls were all developed around the geometry and mechanical behavior of a round workpiece.
“The risk of doing the assembly on the 600mm panel is high, and I don’t think we have all the equipment today to run the process,” said Teck Chong Lee, technical director of advanced fan-out development for HPC applications at ASE, in a recent presentation. “One of the options is, once you complete the interposer in large format in 600, then you divide it into four pieces to run the assembly and the C4 process. This is a much lower-risk approach.”

articles.title: El Niño muda a cor do oceano e ameaça vida marinha
articles.summary:
Imagens de satélite da NASA mostram que partes do Oceano Pacífico passaram de tons esverdeados para um azul mais intenso entre 2025 e 2026. A mudança está associada ao El Niño, fenômeno climático que aquece as águas do oceano e, segundo pesquisadores, está provocando uma redução nas populações de fitoplâncton, organismos microscópicos essenciais para os ecossistemas marinhos.
A alteração foi registrada pelo instrumento Ocean Color Instrument, a bordo do satélite PACE, que monitora variações na luz visível para analisar a distribuição desses organismos. O evento atual pode se tornar o El Niño mais forte já registrado, com temperaturas no Pacífico tropical cerca de 4 °C acima do normal, segundo o artigo publicado pelo site IFLScience.
Por que o oceano está ficando mais azul?
O fitoplâncton reúne milhares de espécies de organismos microscópicos que realizam fotossíntese e produzem diferentes pigmentos, responsáveis por parte das variações de cor dos oceanos. Na região equatorial do Pacífico, espécies verdes ricas em clorofila costumam ser predominantes.
Esses organismos dependem de águas mais frias e ricas em nutrientes. Durante o El Niño, o aquecimento da superfície do oceano reduz a subida de águas profundas que transportam esses nutrientes, prejudicando o desenvolvimento do fitoplâncton.
Os dados do satélite PACE permitem observar essa mudança. Tons mais azuis geralmente indicam menor concentração de fitoplâncton, enquanto áreas esverdeadas e amareladas sugerem concentrações …

articles.title: AI Changes the Data Interface, Not the Query Engine
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- An AI agent that reads Parquet still depends on an execution engine; AI changes the analytical interface and interpretation layer, not the need for precise computation.
- Separate deterministic computation from probabilistic reasoning. Engines should filter, aggregate, and join, while agents should interpret evidence and communicate conclusions.
- An embedded engine such as DuckDB can be sufficient when the data volume is moderate, the primary consumer is the agent workflow, and writes are controlled.
- A managed lakehouse becomes valuable when data has multiple independent consumers, must join with large shared datasets, requires concurrent writes, or needs organization-wide governance.
- Production-grade agent analytics should retain the source data, configuration, derived facts, and model outputs so that every report can be validated and replayed.
AI agents can now generate analytical code, read files from object storage, and turn operational data into structured reports. Does that make data lakes, lakehouses, and SQL engines obsolete? We encountered this question while automating the analysis of a large disaster-recovery exercise. Our first working design stored thirty-second service metrics as Parquet in S3-compatible object storage, used DuckDB for deterministic aggregation, and asked an AI agent to classify failover outcomes and explain the evidence. Buscar una tarifa de luz más económica es el primer paso para reducir la factura, pero puede que aunque tengas contratado el mejor plan sigas pagando de más por otro lado: tu comunidad de vecinos. Es normal que no prestemos mucha atención a estas facturas porque total, se pagan entre todos, pero según un análisis de la OCU al cabo del año puede ser un pico.
Qué ha analizado la OCU. Lo ha hecho la OCU a partir de facturas de comunidades de propietarios, 85 de electricidad y 15 de gas natural, todas ellas dentro del mercado libre. Lo que han visto es que la mayoría de comunidades tenían contratadas tarifas poco competitivas y más potencia de la necesaria en la electricidad.
Lo que se paga de más por la luz. La OCU ha calculado que el sobrecoste en la factura por no tener una tarifa competitiva puede alcanzar los 1.500 euros al año, tomando como modelo una comunidad con 6,94kW contratados y 5.500 kWh de consumo. El precio de la energía no es el único problema, también está el de la potencia contratada. Un 84% de las facturas analizadas pecaban de este problema y el sobrecoste puede llegar a ser de 314 euros más.
El gas natural no se queda atrás. Esto es para la electricidad, pero en el caso del gas natural para edificios con calefacción central el sobrecoste es aún más alto. De media, hay comunidades pagando hasta 3.515 euros al año de más, todo por no tener contratada la tarifa más económica que es la Tarifa de Últim…

articles.title: Panne Orange : voici comment l'opérateur va dédommager ses clients

Concrètement, un abonné disposant d’un forfait de 100 Go bénéficiera de 200 Go le mois suivant son prochain renouvellement.
La panne, qui a débuté vers 11h20 mercredi 21 octobre, a privé des centaines de milliers d’abonnés Orange et Sosh d’appels, de SMS et d’Internet mobile partout en France. « La situation a commencé à revenir à la normale autour de 19h », précise Orange, qui a annoncé un rétablissement complet des clients touchés à 21h. Soit près de dix heures de perturbations pour les abonnés les plus longuement concernés.
Un équipement du nouveau cœur de réseau en cause
Orange lève aussi le voile sur l’origine de la panne. « Cet incident technique a eu lieu sur un équipement de notre nouveau cœur de réseau qui a impacté une partie de nos abonnés sur le territoire », explique l’opérateur, qui écarte explicitement la piste d’une cyberattaque comme celle d’un lien avec une faille PHP, évoquées sur les réseaux sociaux. Le cœur de réseau désigne l’ensemble des serveurs qui authentifient les cartes SIM et acheminent les communications : lorsqu’il fléchit, les téléphones ne peuvent plus se connecter, même si les antennes fonctionnent.

Happy Pay provides zero-cost installment payments through its ad-subsidised payments network. Its platform connects merchants with high-intent shoppers, enabling consumers to split purchases into interest-free installments while helping retailers grow through performance-based customer acquisition, conversion, and basket expansion. The company raised a US$5 million seed round back in March.
Happy Ads lets brands promote products and offers to Happy Pay’s more than 800,000 registered users, as well as two million customers across its partner network. When we published our review of the iPhone Duo, I got a lot of hopeful questions from my fellow Mini fans who took note of the cover screen’s Mini-ish 5.4-inch size. “Is this… a small phone that turns into a tablet?” they asked. And I’m sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but no. The Duo is not the small phone we’ve been looking for.
No, the iPhone Duo isn’t a small phone
This isn’t the iPhone Mini successor we’ve been dreaming of.
I wish it was. I like a small phone. I own an iPhone 13 Mini that I refuse to surrender, even though it barely lasts a full day.
But the Duo is thick and heavy. You will feel its weight every time you read an email, scroll Instagram, or put it in your pocket. It is a dense phone, and after a week with the Duo, my 13 Mini feels almost comically light. Like, can this be a real phone? Surely not.
The Duo’s front panel is also quite a bit wider than the 13 Mini — 84.1mm compared to 64.2mm — which makes it much harder to reach your thumb all the way across like you can with the Mini. As reported by Wired, Apple is also planning to add its reachability feature to the Duo later this year to help out in those moments. But inevitably there’s something I need to tap that’s out of one-handed reach on the Duo, and the illusion of using a small phone is gone. articles.title: Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman says its AI outperforms doctors on hard cases as he chases ‘medical superintelligence’ | TechCrunch

Microsoft’s AI diagnostic system correctly diagnosed complex medical cases in a simulation more than twice as often as generalist physicians, according to a study published Thursday in Science. Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft AI’s CEO, called the result a step toward “medical superintelligence.”
The system, dubbed MAI-DxO (DxO for short), coordinates several AI agents that act like a panel of doctors. They question a patient, order tests, and debate a diagnosis.
In a simulation using complex cases from the New England Journal of Medicine, it was correct 83% of the time. Primary care doctors and general internists, working individually with reference materials, were correct 36% of the time. One note: Cases this complex are usually handled by specialists or physician teams, who weren’t part of the comparison.
“There is something very substantial and exciting here,” Dominic King, vice president of Health at Microsoft AI, told TechCrunch. “The biggest challenge in healthcare delivery at the moment is the growing mismatch between demand and supply of medical expertise.”
In publishing these results, Microsoft joins Google and OpenAI in claiming that its AI can match or outperform doctors.
The study’s own data suggests that much of the improvement comes from more powerful underlying AI models, with Microsoft’s orchestration system adding gains on top.

articles.title: Low-carbon concrete could lower emissions before data centres even go online |

Concerns about the environmental impact of data centres have been popping across Canada almost as quickly as the data centres themselves. But what if there was a way to start lowering those emissions even before a facility is turned on? According to two cleantech advocates, greening the data centre boom starts with the buildings, and the huge amounts of concrete used to create them.
Concrete is responsible for roughly eight percent of the world’s carbon emissions, according to a study by Chatham House. Those emissions come primarily from the process of refining cement, the binding agent used in concrete. Traditional cement is created through a combustion process that both directly releases CO2 into the atmosphere and relies heavily on fossil fuels throughout manufacturing.
“If we’re looking at the concrete and steel that’s going to go into this project, we’re looking at somewhere between 218,000 and 263,000 tonnes of CO2.”
Gil Yaron, Light House
Data centres use a lot of concrete. According to Gil Yaron, the managing director of circular innovation at Light House, a Vancouver-based non-profit supporting regenerative building practices, Meta’s Sturgeon County data centre is predicted to require as much as 1.5 million cubic metres of concrete. That’s roughly the equivalent of 37 CN Towers.
Far from just an enormous physical footprint, that translates into a lot of emissions, according to Yaron.

articles.title: Amazon says PHP2Shell exploitation began 4 days before patches
articles.summary:
Security researchers at Amazon Threat Intelligence say attackers began targeting the PHP2Shell flaws four days before security patches were released on Wednesday.
Tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, the two critical vulnerabilities let attackers gain remote code execution (RCE) on vulnerable systems. The PHP security team patched them on October 21 after urging admins one day earlier to prepare to install the updates as soon as they became available.
PHP core developer Gina Peter Banyard warned before disclosure that applying the official security patches is the only permanent defense, while the UK National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) asked UK organizations to immediately update PHP servers or take them offline until they can be patched.
The PHP team says that everything went according to plan until two days before the coordinated disclosure, when it had to speed up the targeted release date starting October 20 after some details on the PHP2Shell security flaws (including the two CVE IDs and mitigation advice provided to some critical infrastructure providers) leaked online.
While some proof of concepts were also published before patches were released, the PHP security team said none were functional.
Amazon Threat Intelligence's report comes after multiple cybersecurity companies (including Cloudflare, watchTowr, Previdian, Hadrian, and Patchstack) detected unsuccessful exploitation attempts before public disclosure.

The vulnerabilities, collectively dubbed PHP2Shell, could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code on affected servers. Major technology companies have been racing to protect users, with Cloudflare deploying firewall protections and Automattic confirming that websites hosted across its platforms, including WordPress.com, WordPress VIP and Tumblr, have been secured. The Wikimedia Foundation, meanwhile, took several supporting services offline until they can be patched.
The PHP project released emergency fixes on Wednesday for versions 8.2 through 8.5. Older versions are no longer officially supported, although some distributions and vendors provide legacy fixes, and PHP has published limited patches for versions 7.4 through 8.1.

articles.title: New Serious PHP Vulnerabilities Released and Patched - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
New Serious PHP Vulnerabilities Released and Patched
PHP maintainers have released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities:
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately.
Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.
The vulnerabilities:
- RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.
- RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.
Updating PHP is the only way to regain security. Do it now.

Per LiteLLM’s investigation, the attackers obtained the GitHub CLI OAuth tokens for “an unexpected, innocuously named user account in our internal LiteLLM deployment, which was exposed to the public internet”.

As monolithic designs become more difficult and costly to advance, chiplets, advanced packaging, and 3D integration enable higher levels of performance, bandwidth, and functional integration for AI and high-performance computing (HPC) systems.

articles.title: Compromised TLS Certificates - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Compromised TLS Certificates
The Indian CA eMudhra Limited has eight TLS certificates with laughably weak private keys:
The compromised eMudhra keys were defective at a level that’s challenging the imagination of many of the engineers studying the incident. A normal size for a NIST P-384 elliptic curve cryptography private key contains roughly 384 bits of entropy, a size allowing almost 2384, or a number with 116 digits, different possibilities. The private key sizes of the compromised keys ranged from 3 to 8 bits. Astonishingly, the private keys were 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, 237.
“That is extremely in the ‘this should not be possible’ category,” Valdorda said. “Maybe some horribly dangerous key generation interface has a ‘size’ parameter and they set it to 1 by mistake???”
Ben Cartwright-Cox, director of BGP.tools, said: “My guess is that it’s example code that accidentally leaked to production, but hard to know. But it’s bonkers that no one noticed.”
At this early stage, the most immediate threat appears to be for those using VPNs, especially in countries with governments likely to maliciously intercept traffic. There are likely many other cases for concern. End users largely have no recourse other than to hold off using many non-browser forms of TLS communication until they receive assurances updates are in place.
The whole certificate regime has long been a mess:
The incident is the latest to expose a fatal flaw in the TLS regimen. It’s only as strong as its weakest…

articles.title: Who on-calls an AI? This is the unresolved crisis of agent ownership
articles.summary:
Who on-calls an AI? This is the unresolved crisis of agent ownership
At 2:07 a.m., an AI agent starts failing.
The application is still running, but requests are timing out because a downstream API is returning errors. The agent has already retried twice, using more tokens than usual, and its response time has roughly doubled.
The first question should not be:
	“Which model should we use?”
It should be:
	“Who owns this system right now?”
That question is easy to overlook when building AI agents. Teams often pour effort into prompts, retrieval, tools, and model selection, but production ownership determines whether an agent becomes a dependable service or another source of operational risk.
“Teams often pour effort into prompts, retrieval, tools, and model selection, but production ownership determines whether an agent becomes a dependable service or another source of operational risk.”
A production agent needs an owner, boundaries, telemetry, failure policies, escalation paths, and a clear distinction between what the system may automate and what requires human intervention.
A production agent should not have a direct path from reasoning to action. Each tool invocation should pass through explicit controls, remain observable, and have a defined path to human intervention.
Here’s a practical way to build those controls.
Step 1: Treat the agent as a production service
An agent should have the same operational identity as any other production service.

After decades in philanthropy, Derek Lubner discovered that giving money was simple; verifying where it went was the real challenge. In conversation with PHATHISANI MOYO, the iZinga Assist co-founder explains how he plans to repair the trust deficit between donors and grassroots NGOs.
When Derek Lubner was managing his late parents’ foundation, Make an Immediate Difference, he routinely asked beneficiary non-profit organisations to submit wish lists for the upcoming year.
If an organisation wanted cricket bats and nets, a classroom or a soccer field, the co-founder and chairman of iZinga Assist, digital non-profit verification and support platform, would consider the request and agree to fund all or part of it. His only condition was that the organisation send him a photograph showing what the money had paid for.
Over the years, he estimates that barely a quarter of the organisations ever sent the requested pictures, leaving him with no straightforward way to confirm whether the equipment had been purchased or the project delivered.
For someone dedicated to supporting grassroots community initiatives across South Africa, the omission was frustrating. Yet it also forced him to reconsider the administrative burden traditional donors impose on frontline social workers.
“I could have blamed the organisations and cut their funding,” Lubner told TechCabal. “Instead, I realised we needed to help them meet those compliance requirements.”
That conviction spurred the creation of iZinga…

articles.title: Es oficial: 'Carrie' tendrá segunda temporada en Prime Video

Era solo cuestión de tiempo hasta que se anunciara, y ya es oficial: Carrie regresará a Prime Video con una segunda temporada. La aclamada serie de Mike Flanagan, basada en la obra homónima de Stephen King, expandirá su adaptación televisiva con más episodios que irán más allá de los eventos contemplados dentro del libro original.
Amazon MGM Studios lo hizo oficial a través de su blog oficial, apenas un par de semanas después de que la primera temporada de Carrie cosechara excelentes críticas tanto del público como la prensa especializada, convirtiéndose además en uno de los títulos originales más exitosos de Prime Video.

Si bien la nueva serie de Carrie cubre los eventos del libro de Stephen King al completo, su conclusión dejaba abierta la puerta a una posible continuación. Es posible que su concreción o no estuviese vinculada con la recepción que lograra tanto en críticas como en cantidad de espectadores, por lo que no sorprende esta renovación para una segunda temporada.

articles.title: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up.
Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials.
The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents, accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand.
1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. The company says it is working with other companies to expand the service.
“Handing over a password, secret, or credential is a common shortcut to an agent, but can leave people with sensitive information in places they can no longer control as a copy gets saved for the next time,” the company said in a blog post. “1Password for Agents gives people a trusted way to delegate task…

articles.title: MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells
articles.summary:
MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells
- Date:
- October 23, 2026
- Source:
- Massachusetts Institute of Technology
- Summary:
- MIT engineers have built a paper-thin swimming robot powered by living muscle cells that respond to flashes of light, allowing it to swim and steer through water. The breakthrough could pave the way for tiny, self-healing biological robots capable of exploring fragile environments that ordinary machines cannot safely navigate.
- Share:
A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.
The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. The gel forms two fins, each coated with a layer of muscle cells far thinner than a human hair. These cells have been genetically modified to contract when exposed to light.
By directing light onto either fin, the researchers can trigger muscle contractions that make the fin flap and push the robot through water. Adjusting which fin receives light and how frequently it is illuminated allows the team to control both its speed and direction.

articles.title: Quest Diagnostics Reports Cyber Breach Affecting ‘Certain Patient Records’
articles.summary:
Medical laboratory operator Quest Diagnostics said it learned of a cyber breach of one of its systems this week, likely compromising some records for patients.
In a Thursday regulatory filing, Quest Diagnostics reported “unauthorized access” to its Quanum Lab Services Manager, a platform where certain clients can place test orders and receive or look up their results. The company said it discovered the hack on Wednesday and notified federal law enforcement.
How many patients and which particular records have been affected is still unknown. Quest Diagnostics said it believes “certain patient records” were accessed in the breach, but that the full scope remains under investigation.
The New Jersey-based company said it’s also working with external cybersecurity experts to assist in its response.
Quest Diagnostics has seen hacks impacting patient records before. In 2016, for example, the company said data including lab results and contact information of about 34,000 people was exposed in another online breach. And in 2019, other personal information belonging to about 11.9 million Quest patients was affected after a separate hack at American Medical Collection Agency, a billing collections service provider.
Cyberattacks are on the rise across industries. Beyond healthcare, other breaches have recently disrupted anything from supermarket chains to core education applications.

articles.title: Study Finds AI-generated Code Fails to Boost Productivity Due to Downstream Bottlenecks
articles.summary:
A recent Harvard study of 718 firms, using the Jellyfish analytics platform, finds that although AI coding assistants and agents increase code volume, this does not translate into a corresponding increase in completed work, partly because AI-generated code increases the workload in later stages of development, particularly code review.
The study was based on approximately 300 million work events of 700,000 workers across 700+ firms from January 2021 to March 2026. The data was gathered from several sources such as HR information, code version control systems, issue management systems, scheduling tools such as Google Calendar, and generative-AI tools, including GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code.
The researchers considered three measures of coding output: lines of code added, commits, and pull requests.
AI assistants lead to small increases in code output — 12% for lines of code, 9% for commits, and 5% for pull requests — with only the effect on commits being statistically significant. AI agents lead to large and significant increases in all three measures: 30% for lines of code, 20% for commits, and 23% for pull requests.
The authors used these data to evaluate software output by the number of Jira issues and epics resolved per worker per month, with issues treated as individual units of engineering work, and epics as larger projects or features.
