articles.title: Microsoft shares how to fix broken Exchange Online EWS apps
articles.summary:
Microsoft says IT admins can re-enable the retired Exchange Web Services (EWS) API in Exchange Online to fix EWS apps that have stopped working.
EWS is an API for developing apps that can access Exchange mailbox items (e.g., email messages, meetings, and contacts) from Exchange Online and on-premises Exchange servers.
This API is used by various apps, including but not limited to Outlook desktop add-ins, older versions of Outlook for Windows, the Apple Mail / Calendar on macOS, and various other apps.
In February, the company announced it will start blocking the EWS API by default on October 1, 2026, but will let IT administrators temporarily maintain access via an app allowlist until the final shutdown on April 1, 2027. However, when EWS is disabled, the apps show errors ranging from alerts that the EWS protocol is unavailable to repeated prompts to enter the username or password.
To avoid these issues and fix EWS apps that are no longer working, Microsoft says tenant administrators can re-enable EWS in the Microsoft 365 admin center Baseline Security Mode by unchecking "Block your entire organization from using EWS" on the Baseline Security Mode page.
Another option is to use Exchange Online PowerShell to run the "Set-OrganizationConfig -EWSEnabled $true" command, which should re-enable EWS within 4 hours.
"We are now in the first stage of EWS disablement, where customers are still able to re-enable EWS. Re-enabling EWS will stop working in April 2027," Microsoft said.

articles.title: Retro gaming is being overrun with AI
articles.summary:
Retro video games are everywhere lately — especially in places where they aren’t supposed to be. Halo in a web browser, Wind Waker on the iPhone, Super Smash Bros. in mixed reality. Over the past month or so, these kinds of unexpected projects have gone viral with incredible frequency thanks to new AI tools, as hobbyists take apart games and then rebuild them for new platforms. But while AI has supercharged the pace of these ports, it’s also tearing apart tight-knit communities dedicated to preserving games.
Retro gaming is being overrun with AI
A rise in AI-powered decomps, recomps, and ports has thrust the community into chaos.
Decomps and recomps — shorthand for decomposition and recomposition — are a form of reverse engineering that involves breaking a game down to its building blocks and then rebuilding it so it can run on hardware it was never intended for. When done manually, it’s a slow, painstaking process. A group spent years decompiling the original Animal Crossing on the GameCube, for instance. But AI coding tools have cut that timeline down significantly, and the sheer number of ports has grown dramatically in recent months.
This summer, Chris Sotraidis, an AI consultant who works on game ports as a hobby, saw a port of Command & Conquer: Generals Zero Hour — which EA made open source last year — for the iPhone and iPad. The “technical challenges” inspired him to try making a handful of similar ports, including a mobile port of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Tim…

Stop guessing auto scaling targets for TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI
A traffic spike hits your self-hosted text-to-speech (TTS) endpoint, and requests start queueing. Latency climbs past your service level objective (SLO) right when the most callers are listening. The auto scaling policy behind that endpoint was supposed to prevent this, but the target value it scales on was a guess, and guesses like that fail silently until real traffic proves them wrong.
Get that number wrong, and it’s paid for in one of two ways, and neither shows up as an alarm. Guess too conservative, and the fleet runs GPU instances that sit mostly idle. That cost lands on every invoice but never trips an incident report. Guess too aggressive, and the fleet carries a risk nobody sees. Each instance holds more concurrent requests than it can serve inside its latency promise. Nothing looks wrong until a real traffic spike pushes queueing time past the SLO. That happens right when the most callers are listening. That’s the hidden gap. A policy that looks fine on the console can already be failing the people it’s supposed to serve.
In this post, we deploy Kokoro-82M, an 82-million-parameter TTS model, as a custom container on an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint. AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) stacks handle the deployment. We replace guesswork with two measurements taken against the live endpoint. articles.title: How Self-Aligned CFET Technology Could Extend CMOS Scaling Beyond 10 Å
articles.summary:
A process sequence for SRAM and logic that delivers higher performance through larger effective channel width and improved electrostatics at smaller nodes.
As their dimensions continue to shrink, conventional gate-all-around (GAA) nanosheet transistors may face growing challenges, such as leakage, mobility, resistance, and manufacturing variability.
A proposed self-aligned complementary field-effect transistor (SA-CFET) architecture addresses these constraints by vertically stacking N-channel metal-oxide-semiconductor (NMOS) and P-channel metal-oxide-semiconductor (PMOS) devices and using self-aligned modules to improve density and manufacturability.
A complementary field-effect transistor (CFET) is a transistor architecture that vertically stacks NMOS and PMOS devices. This configuration can reduce cell area, increase effective channel width, and improve electrostatic control compared with side-by-side device layouts.
With SEMulator3D, the Semiverse Solutions team used digital twin process modeling to show that the self-aligned architecture can support static random-access memory (SRAM) and logic cells while delivering a 0.0094 μm² SRAM bit cell, a 52.7% area reduction compared with N3 technology, and at least a 10 nm overlay window across critical contact layers.

articles.title: AI found a critical PHP flaw. The bigger failure began in 2024.
articles.summary:
AI found a critical PHP flaw. The bigger failure began in 2024.
Did one of your favorite websites go dark on Wednesday? Some did, as operators took services offline while they waited for fixes to two critical flaws in PHP, the language behind much of the web.
The precaution didn’t mean those sites were hacked. The holes themselves were bad news with a capital B. But the bigger long-term concern might be how the embargo on the patches was handled.
PHP powers roughly 70% of websites, but that figure describes PHP’s reach, not the number of vulnerable or compromised sites.
WordPress told site owners to update PHP; these flaws don’t require a WordPress update.
The flaws are CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The PHP project’s fixed releases are 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12; users of older PHP branches need a supported upgrade or a distributor’s backport.
The PHP security emergency, aka PHP2Shell, exposed more than dangerous bugs in a widely used language. The release also set off a dispute over coordinated disclosure and underscored the pressure on open-source maintainers as AI-assisted researchers find and develop exploits faster.
The road to this emergency ran through OpenAI’s Patch the Planet initiative. Working in that program, security firm Calif used GPT-5.6 Sol to find a route to remote code execution and reported it to PHP on August 11. OpenAI independently reported the same underlying issue that day; Wiz reported its findings on August 24. PHP’s maintainers led th…

- Anthropic used Claude to analyze 25 open source projects and uncovered nearly 500 security issues
- Research found exposed pre-authentication code paths, conflicting security settings, and long-hidden flaws
- AI identified attack-surface reductions that removed unnecessary code exposure before vulnerabilities could be exploited
Anthropic recently used Claude to analyze 25 major open source projects written in C, C++, Java, PHP, and Python, in search of security issues. It found almost 500 of them, including security controls turned off by conflicts in settings, sensitive code accessible before authentication, and even a vulnerability that sat in the code for 21 years.
This wasn’t a standard hunt for vulnerabilities. In its report, Anthropic argues that looking for individual vulnerabilities is a Sisyphean task that scales poorly and never guarantees security. Instead, it thinks defenders should turn towards reducing software attack surfaces by restricting unnecessary access to potentially exploitable code.
“A defender who reduces unnecessary attack surface in their code reduces the risk from all of the unknown vulnerabilities in that code at once—including any that are already being quietly exploited,” Anthropic said.

Japanese gaming company Capcom has disclosed a data breach impacting 11 million email addresses and the personal information of a small number of individuals.
The incident, the gaming giant says, was discovered on October 19 and involved unauthorized access to CAPCOM ID, its shared service used for accessing online services and for playing online games.
During the intrusion, the hackers stole the email addresses of 11,774,247 people, along with account data such as creation date, last login date, number of logins, and the last login’s IP address.
For 43 of the affected customers, the hackers also compromised dates of birth, gender information, country/region details, and nicknames.
Additionally, Capcom determined that the attackers changed the CAPCOM ID account passwords for 196 of the affected users. The company says that no user passwords were compromised and that it has already reset the passwords for the affected accounts.
Capcom says it implemented incident response measures and all services using CAPCOM ID remain available.
“In addition, we have started to contact the target customers sequentially, and we have established a dedicated contact point for customers regarding this matter,” an automated translation of Capcom’s incident notice reads.
The gaming company says it has reported the data breach to the relevant authorities and continues to investigate it.

articles.title: NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular
articles.summary:
NgRx, the reactive state management framework for Angular, has released version 22, shipping utilities for customising Angular's resource API, dynamic deep signals for union types, a new SignalStore typing helper and ESLint v10 compatibility.
The main new addition is resource extensions, delivered through a new experimental @ngrx/signals/resource entry point. Angular's resource and httpResource APIs reset value() to undefined while reloading and throw when read in an error state. Resource extensions wrap an existing resource and patch only those behaviours, while preserving the original resource type.
Four built-in extensions are included, alongside a provideResourceExtensions function that registers defaults at application, route or component level. In the original RFC, Marko Stanimirović explained that changing the error behaviour is also a prerequisite for deeper SignalStore integration, as "once a resource enters the error state, any subsequent patchState call will throw because it reads value() internally".
The proposal was well received, with Manfred Steyer replying "Love it!" and suggesting an activation signal, while another commenter asked for parity with SolidJS's createResource, such as access to the current value inside the loader.
A community roundup on DEV noted that similar behaviour could be built with Angular's snapshot() and extra state logic, but "with Resource Extensions, you stay on the resource itself", keeping the value writable and retaining the more s…

Arista Networks released security updates to patch an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability affecting VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) On-Prem deployments.
VCO is a web-based management portal that helps administrators configure, monitor, and manage VeloCloud SD-WANs (Software-Defined Wide Area Networks) and associated edge devices.
Tracked as CVE-2026-114625, this critical-severity flaw can allow attackers with basic privileges, access to the VCO web interface, and a valid authenticated session to escalate privileges through low-complexity SQL injection attacks that don't require user interaction.
"VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) on-prem has a security issue where this issue may allow a remote attacker to access privileged internal functionality and impact the VCO host. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and data managed by the orchestrator," Arista said.
"On an affected system, any authenticated user can gain operator privileges and masquerade as a local 'superuser operator' user. This includes access to functionality that is intended for internal use only and which is not intended to be remotely accessible."
The company said it has already patched hosted VCO deployments running version 5.2.3.18 or later, 6.1.3.10 or later, and 6.4.2.12 or later.

articles.title: LTO roadmap extends to 365 TB per cartridge as tape storage refuses to die — AI boom spurs relevance of cheap, airgapped storage
articles.summary:
LTO roadmap extends to 365 TB per cartridge as tape storage refuses to die —25-year-old format sees 400x capacity increase without changing form factor
HPE, IBM, and Quantum will keep developing LTO as demand booms.
In a world where SSDs with up to 256TB capacity are about to enter the scene to compete against hard disk drives that store over 40TB, magnetic tape storage may seem archaic. However, the 25-year-old Linear Tape-Open (LTO) format continues to evolve at a rather impressive pace.
The current LTO-10 generation stores up to 40TB of uncompressed data per cartridge, while HPE, IBM, and Quantum — the companies behind the LTO Program — now envision LTO-14 cartridges with up to 365TB of native capacity. But capacity is not the only advantage of LTO. In fact, the consortium has deliberately slowed its capacity roadmap in a bid to prioritize reliability, cost per terabyte, and manageable backup and recovery times over the previous goal of doubling capacity with every generation.
LTO began in 2000 with the LTO-1 format, which stored just 100GB of data natively and transferred it at 20 MB/s. Since then, capacity increased to 200GB with LTO-2, 400GB with LTO-3, 800GB with LTO-4, 1.5TB with LTO-5, 2.5TB with LTO-6, 6TB with LTO-7, 12TB with LTO-8, and 18TB with LTO-9.
The original LTO-10 media introduced in 2025 increased native capacity to 30TB, whereas an extended-length LTO-10 cartridge announced later increased it further to 40TB.

articles.title: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories
articles.summary:
Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight.
AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load.
The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production.
Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory
Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads.
With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

At this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt, Lovable go-to-market lead Luke Arno, Ben Broca of the AI platform Polsia, and Theory Ventures’ Tomasz Tunguz gave founders some tips on how to set their companies up for success in those first 90 days.
Broca, whose company Polsia uses AI agents to build and run businesses with almost no human staff (Broca says he is its only employee), said that product-market fit is one of the hardest things to find right now, especially in an era when so many products can easily be copied by competitors. In response, Arno said that durable go-to-market strategies are those that can be reliably repeated.
“The most critical thing for founders or earlier-stage companies to do is develop learning density or pattern recognition for where your customers are,” Arno said. “Don’t rush to build out a top-down go-to-market motion if you’re not there yet.”

articles.title: Stream low-latency speech from AI agents using Kokoro TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Stream low-latency speech from AI agents using Kokoro TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI
A customer asks an AI voice agent a question and waits. The agent already has an answer, it’s midway through generating a long, multi-paragraph response, but the customer hears nothing for five seconds. By the time an answer arrives, the customer is frustrated, confused, and no longer paying attention.
Text-to-speech integrations create exactly that gap. A one-sentence response might generate in 600 milliseconds, but the full response takes five seconds, and the integration waits for all of it before synthesis starts.
This post shows how to close that gap. We stream each sentence to a hosted Kokoro-82M text-to-speech (TTS) model on Amazon SageMaker AI as soon as an agent produces it, so synthesis begins on sentence one instead of the finished response. Getting that audio back to a browser needs its own solution too, so we also cover both transports for doing it and what each costs in practice.
Solution overview
This solution closes the gap by streaming synthesis alongside generation instead of waiting for it to finish. As the agent produces each sentence, that sentence streams immediately to a hosted Kokoro-82M text-to-speech model, so audio playback can start before the agent finishes speaking its full response. Millicent Okumu doesn’t leave you wondering whether she believes what she is saying. She speaks with energy, with clarity about whom she is building for. Ask where the company is heading, and there is little hesitation; ask whether she will still be running it in ten years, and the answer is no.
By then, she expects Agriflex, the Kenyan agricultural business she co-founded, to be operating in at least five African countries, to be sustainably profitable, and to be led by somebody else. She might take an advisory role. For now, however, the company occupies even the hours she supposedly spends away from it. At family gatherings, unfinished tasks follow her into the room.
Her father, a civil servant and farmer, raised cattle and grew enough food to support relatives beyond his household. She was close to him, but less enthusiastic about the farm. She avoided agriculture at school and university, only to find herself back in it through a logistics job at iProcure in 2017.
Now she sells farm inputs, deploys spraying drones and listens to farmers explain why a clever piece of technology might be of little use to them. That last part has meant slowing down plans and turning away investors.
“We are in 2026,” she says. “We are no longer in 2006.”
She is impatient for progress, but increasingly particular about what counts as progress, and who benefits.

articles.title: LiteLLM release pipeline hacked to distribute info-stealer malware

Hackers compromised the LiteLLM project’s PyPI package and published malicious Docker images with a payload that steals credentials, secrets, and environment variables.
The supply-chain attack affected all PyPI wheels (.whl installation packages) for LiteLLM version 1.107.0, impacting Windows, Linux, and macOS systems.
LiteLLM is an open-source Python SDK and AI gateway that enables applications to access AI models from different providers through a common API.
It is a massively popular project with 61,800 GitHub stars, 92 million monthly downloads on PyPI, and is used by high-profile companies like NVIDIA, Netflix, AT&T, and Okta.
The project says that the release pipeline was compromised on October 21 and a threat actor pushed version 1.107.0 to the Docker registry and PyPI.
"This version contained compiled malware which steals credentials and loads remote-code execution tools," the maintainer says, adding that customers running the private enterprise were not impacted.
In a post-mortem of the incident, the maintainer says that the following LiteLLM artifacts were affected in the attack:
- PyPI: litellm==1.107.0: all seven wheels, live from 11:39:51 to 13:23 UTC
- Docker Hub: v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, and main-stable: pointed to compromised image index sha256:1bbcb1443bc962e45f5aad53fe3d2c30600e0379715fb6c664cdd3ac126c339e from 11:46:56 to 14:20 UTC

articles.title: eMudhra to exit global website security certificate business

eMudhra to exit global website security certificate business
The move follows scrutiny over weak cryptographic keys, with eMudhra citing rising compliance costs and declining returns from a business that contributes just 1% of its revenue.
Bengaluru-based digital trust company eMudhra has decided to exit its global SSL/TLS certificate business following a security incident involving weak cryptographic keys that prompted action from Google and Mozilla. In a regulatory filing on Thursday, the company said its board had decided to voluntarily withdraw from the business, citing rising compliance costs, increasing data sovereignty requirements and diminishing commercial returns. The decision follows the discovery of eight intermediate certificate authority keys linked to eMudhra that were found to be dangerously weak, potentially allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate websites. The keys were generated in April 2025, but the weakness remained undetected for about 18 months. Google and Mozilla subsequently moved to block the affected certificates to protect users. eMudhra Chairman V Srinivasan said the company had revoked the affected certificate authorities within 14 hours of discovering the incident and promptly disclosed the issue.
The company maintained that its infrastructure had not been compromised, no data had been breached and none of the affected intermediate authorities had issued end-user certificates.

The apps parents download are fun, but they teach their own course, not the one the child is tested on. And nobody – teacher, principal or parent – sees how a child is doing until the exam. Founded in Assiut in Upper Egypt, Learning Rockets launched the first prototype of its Bee Degree app in 2023, with the idea for the business having started at home.

Deploy AI in a HIPAA-eligible environment with Amazon Quick
Healthcare organizations want the same thing from AI that every other business wants: faster answers, less manual work, and insights that reach decision-makers in time to act on them. However, what makes the healthcare industry different is that the data is uniquely complex, deeply contextual, and strictly regulated. So this post starts with a few definitions to set the foundation for everything that follows.
Protected Health Information (PHI) is any information that identifies a person and relates to their health, care, or payment for care, such as a medical note, a claim, or a member ID. When software touches PHI, it falls under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), the federal law that governs how PHI data is accessed, secured, and audited.
Agentic AI changes what it means for software to “touch PHI.” A traditional analytics tool reads data and returns a response. An agentic workspace like Amazon Quick might go further. For example, its chat agents work across both unstructured content, such as clinical notes and appeals letters, and structured data, such as claims and member records. Los motivos por los que te estancas. Cuando hacemos ejercicio, experimentamos efectos inmediatos y a largo plazo. articles.title: Ink droplets in motion snag top prize in Nikon Small World contest
articles.summary:
A 25-year-old German experimental photographer has won the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition with a striking image of droplets of ink being deposited on paper by an inkjet printer. Ole Bielfeldt beat out 1,802 other entries hailing from 69 different countries.
Bielfeldt became interested in photomicrography during the COVID-19 lockdown after discovering an old microscope in his parents’ attic. He figured out how to build an adaptor out of a tube and some wood to connect the microscope to his father’s camera and taught himself the art through trial and error, building custom tools as needed. He documents how he captures transformative images of everyday objects with behind-the-scenes videos posted to macrofying, his photography and videography brand.
It was Bielfeldt’s curiosity about the inner workings of inkjet printers that inspired his winning entry, but capturing the action of ink drops being deposited on paper was a challenge, given that the process happens so quickly. The droplets, for instance, moved faster than the camera’s shutter speed. Bielfeldt’s solution was to deconstruct the printer so that the paper moved under a stationary (rather than moving) printhead, and then take the image in a dark room, using a flash to serve as the shutter, thereby freezing the ink drops mid-air. There was no need for pricey equipment. Bielfeldt does not use AI in his images, preferring to rely on traditional techniques.

Artificial Intelligence
Write your own training loop — without managing GPUs — with Amazon SageMaker training session APIs
Fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) today usually forces a tradeoff between training loop control and operational simplicity. With fully managed services you select a base model, provide data and hyperparameters, and the service owns everything else, which works well when a standard, prepackaged recipe fits your problem. Less managed services give you more control, but you also manage more of the underlying infrastructure and training frameworks. Sometimes a standard recipe isn’t enough: you need a custom loss or data curriculum for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), your own preference optimization, a reinforcement learning (RL) reward function, or an alignment algorithm published last week. As soon as you need to shape the training procedure yourself, you take on that infrastructure work to gain algorithmic freedom.
Today, serverless model customization in Amazon SageMaker AI expands with training session APIs, which remove that tradeoff by drawing the abstraction boundary one level lower. Instead of abstracting away the algorithm, they abstract away the compute. articles.title: Multi-Cloud FinOps: An Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Cloud providers in multi-cloud systems charge for data leaving their network, not entering it. The egress costs accumulate silently and are rarely caught before deployment.
- Architecture determines egress cost more than per-unit transfer rates. Where services are placed and how often they communicate matters far more than what you negotiate on billing rates.
- FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) provides a unified billing format across cloud providers, reducing normalization effort, but service-level attribution still requires provider-specific fields, ownership metadata, and network telemetry.
- Replacing continuous cross-cloud data transfer with scheduled synchronization reduces costs significantly without degrading service performance.
- Architecture had a larger impact on cost than provider pricing. In the controlled experiment, changing the communication pattern from synchronous cross-cloud processing to near-source processing saved over $2000 per month, while changing the provider rate saved $825 per month.
Introduction
Multi-cloud architectures give teams the flexibility to optimize for availability, vendor capabilities, and geographic reach. But this flexibility carries a hidden cost due to data movement across cloud provider boundaries. The costs accumulate through service placement decisions, communication patterns, and scaling behavior compounding over time. By the time it shows up on a bill, the architectural damage is done.

articles.title: PVTW: Extending Silicon Characterization From PVT To Real-World Workload
articles.summary:
Two devices operating at exactly the same voltage, frequency, and temperature can behave differently depending on what they are being asked to do.
For decades, silicon characterization has been built around Process, Voltage, and Temperature, or PVT. We characterize devices across process variation, sweep voltage and frequency, control temperature, generate SHMOO plots, and establish the operating envelope of the silicon.
That methodology remains fundamental. But today’s high-performance processors are increasingly systems in their own right. An AI accelerator may contain thousands of compute elements, distributed SRAM, high-speed SerDes, PCIe and Ethernet interfaces, multiple clock and power domains, advanced packaging, firmware, operating systems, compilers and application software.
This suggests adding another dimension: PVTW: Process × Voltage × Temperature × Workload
Frequency can be swept within this characterization space to determine operating margin.
The objective is not to replace traditional ATE characterization with System Level Test. It is to combine the electrical precision and control available from ATE with the realistic operating environment available from SLT, while retaining the ability to use either independently.
One way to implement PVTW is through a hybrid characterization architecture integrating ATE resources and SLT capability.

A DRAM module or SSD failure in an industrial computer controlling a production line can generate costs far exceeding the price of the component itself, ranging from production downtime and on-site maintenance to the potential loss of critical data.

Una serie de vulnerabilidades críticas en PHP, uno de los lenguajes de programación más utilizados para desarrollar sitios web y aplicaciones, encendió las alertas internacionales de ciberseguridad después de que investigadores identificaran fallos que habrían permanecido ocultos durante años.
El hallazgo, realizado con ayuda de herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA), llevó a gobiernos y organizaciones a recomendar actualizaciones urgentes e incluso la desconexión temporal de algunas plataformas.
Entre los servicios que adoptaron medidas preventivas figuran sitios de Wikimedia, la organización responsable de Wikipedia, además de páginas de organismos públicos de Europa.
En Reino Unido, las autoridades informaron que 32 servicios gubernamentales estaban fuera de servicio en medio de la alerta global, aunque atribuyeron buena parte de las interrupciones a decisiones preventivas y no confirmaron que todos los casos estuvieran directamente relacionados con la explotación de estas vulnerabilidades.
Las empresas de ciberseguridad Wiz y Calif participaron en la investigación de los fallos, mientras que OpenAI confirmó que su tecnología de inteligencia artificial contribuyó a identificar problemas en el código. Los desarrolladores de PHP publicaron actualizaciones para corregir las vulnerabilidades y recomendaron instalarlas cuanto antes.

articles.title: PEGI is giving games with paid loot boxes a PEGI 16 rating, and EA FC 27 is the first big example
articles.summary:
Editor's take: The Europe-based PEGI rating system is introducing a significant change in how games sold across the Old Continent are labelled and marketed to consumers. Digital-only titles designed to sell gamers random items for a pretty penny now face the same rating risks as games depicting violence, sexual activity, and drug use. As they should.
Earlier this year, the Pan-European Game Information (PEGI) system announced a new rating regime for video games built around selling randomized content to players. Now, the organization responsible for administering PEGI in the United Kingdom has confirmed that the changes are finally being implemented. Major game releases have already been affected by the new ratings, although the new rules are expected to remain exclusive to Europe.
According to a recent post by Connor Hinde, who serves as a PEGI administrator in the UK, the Games Rating Authority (GRA) has begun applying the new PEGI rating criteria. A number of previously released, digital-only games will be affected, starting with titles that employ aggressive monetization tactics, such as loot boxes and other systems involving randomized rewards.
A game such as EA Sports FC 27, which previously carried a PEGI 3 rating – meaning it was considered suitable for all ages – has now been assigned a PEGI 16 rating. articles.title: Cloudflare Brings On-Demand CPU and Memory Profiling to Production Workers
articles.summary:
Cloudflare has introduced on-demand CPU and memory profiling for Workers and Durable Objects, allowing developers to investigate performance bottlenecks in production using interactive flamegraphs. Announced on October 9, 2026, the feature generates interactive flamegraphs through the Workers Observability dashboard or the cf CLI, helping teams identify expensive functions and memory allocations without relying solely on logs and aggregate metrics.
Developers can capture CPU or heap-allocation profiles for a deployed Worker version and inspect the results as a flamegraph, where wider sections indicate functions responsible for a larger share of CPU time or sampled memory allocations. Profiles can also be downloaded for offline analysis.
The key distinction is that profiling targets an already-running isolate rather than starting a fresh one. This allows developers to examine code executing under real production traffic. Durable Objects receive additional support for profiling a specific named instance, which is useful when investigating problems tied to stateful workloads. However, the target must receive sufficient traffic during the capture window, and TypeScript developers should enable source maps to make function names easier to interpret.

articles.title: Five AI agent harnesses took the same memory test. The results weren't even close.
articles.summary:
Five AI agent harnesses took the same memory test. The results weren’t even close.
AI agents are getting better at remembering past conversations and earlier tasks but remembering something doesn’t guarantee an agent can use it to do better work next time. Letta’s new FrontierMemory benchmark, released Wednesday, tests that gap by measuring whether agents can learn from experience rather than by just retrieving stored information. Early results show a widespread in performance across agent harnesses, the the infrastructure that manages how an agent operates.
Letta Dream came out on top with a 73.3% score, followed by Prime Agent at 60%. OpenAI Agents SDK scored 40%, while Claude Managed Agents and Hermes Agent trailed at 33.3% and 26.7%, respectively.
Recall isn’t learning
“Modern ‘memory’ benchmarks are saturated since they measure recall of facts,” Letta co-founder and CEO Charles Packer writes on X, saying that in the coding harness and bash loop era, recall is solved, while continual learning in token space, meaning learning through the context an agent keeps rather than through weight updates, remains unsolved.
Sarah Wooders, also a Letta co-founder, points to another problem on X. Most coding and knowledge-work benchmarks evaluate unrelated tasks with all the necessary context provided upfront. But that’s not how people actually work. Wooders compares it to starting a new job: A new hire needs plenty of direction, while someone who’s been there for years can often get t…

In a fireside chat titled "Tool to Co-creator: How AI is rewriting the creative process,” with Aditya Gurwara, Co-Founder and Head of Brand Alliance, Qoruz, Chandrika said that Canva sees itself as "a collaborator, a partner and an enabler" in the creative process. According to her, AI removes barriers of skill, resources, and knowledge.
She drove the point home with an interesting statistic.
“We've heard from 97% of the marketers we have surveyed that they use AI in some form. But it's about understanding whether this is the best output I can get from the prompt I've generated. articles.title: Canadians spent millions on OnlyFans this year, report reveals
articles.summary:
Despite consistent complaints about a tough economy, it turns out that Canadians are more than willing to open their wallets for a little exclusive content.
According to the OnlyFans Wrapped 2026 report from OnlyFinder, Canadians spent a whopping $170.2 million on the platform over the past year. That’s a 16.2 per cent increase from the previous year, more than double the global growth rate of 7.6 per cent.
The amount is also enough to be one small Oceania nation’s total gross domestic product (GDP).
OnlyFinder, an independent search tool unaffiliated with OnlyFans, used search and traffic data to model consumer spending across the platform. Its geographic estimates are based on data and anchored to revenue figures reported by OnlyFans’ parent company, the U.K.-based Fenix International.
Many of us are quick to assume the platform only promotes pornography, which is sort of fair.
“On OnlyFans, adult content and adult searches are well over 50 per cent of total platform usage. So the reputation that OnlyFans skews more towards adult content is accurate,” OnlyFinder CEO Max Anderson tells Daily Hive.
Still, the platform also hosts creators in non-adult niches, including fitness and food, alongside celebrities offering fans exclusive access to their lives — all for a few bucks, of course.
According to the report, those customers aren’t just paying for a monthly subscription.

articles.title: Micron pulls the plug on future 4F² DRAM after two decades of research in dramatic shift — company says architecture offers no meaningful density advantages, increases manufacturing complexity and costs, and has fundamental scaling limitations
articles.summary:
Micron pulls the plug on future 4F² DRAM after two decades of research in dramatic shift — company says architecture offers no meaningful density advantages, increases manufacturing complexity and costs, and has fundamental scaling limitations
Micron goes against the industry?
DRAM featuring 4F² memory cells has long been considered one of the holy grails of the DRAM industry, as they promise to reduce cell area by 33% compared with conventional 6F² designs and therefore enable building DRAMs with more memory cells in the same area. However, after working on 4F² memory cells for a couple of decades, Micron has concluded that the architecture offers no meaningful density advantages, increases manufacturing complexity and costs, and has fundamental scaling limitations. This has a dramatic impact on Micron's future plans.
"Micron invented 4F² DRAM," said Scott DeBoer, president and chief technology and products officer at Micron, during the company's event on Wednesday. "The path with 4F² DRAM is always been an option through time, and we have evaluated it and not pursued it due to increased complexity and cost through this past two-decade period of time."
Interestingly, both Samsung and SK hynix still have 4F² memory cells in their roadmaps (according to TechInsights), so Micron's rejection of the technology puts the company on a unique trajectory. articles.title: As blockchain investing falls out of vogue, a16z Crypto rebrands as a16z Frontier | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
In a sign that crypto and blockchain-focused investing has receded in importance, Andreessen Horowitz announced Thursday that it is renaming its digital asset unit from a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier.
The practice, helmed by Chris Dixon, has raised nearly $10 billion across five funds since launching in 2018, backing some of the sector’s biggest wins, including Coinbase. Yet for years, a16z and rival venture firms struggled to push crypto’s utility beyond financial rails, trading applications, and speculative assets.
Under the new name, the team is broadening its mandate to focus on emerging technologies, be it AI, robotics, or “new kinds of networks” connecting humans and machines. Yet, the group isn’t abandoning crypto. Dixon wrote in a blog post that blockchain technology could “give new networks native economic capabilities.”
Alongside Dixon, a16z Frontier’s general partners include Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet. Meanwhile, Ali Yahya, who joined the crypto strategy as its first investor in 2017, has left the firm, according to The Information.

articles.title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
articles.summary:
eMudhra, the certificate authority that issued eight intermediate TLS credentials so weak that anyone could mint certificates for any website or mail server—one had a private encryption key of just 4—said it’s getting out of the business.
V. Srinivasan, chairman of India-based eMudhra Limited, cited increasing costs and complexities of compliance requirements—paired with the business generating just 1 percent of its revenue. He also said that the emergence of organizations providing TLS certificates free of charge further reduced returns on investment when compared to other products and services the company offers.
Don’t let the door hit you on the butt
“However, the level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business,” the company continued in a Thursday post. “In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders.”
The announcement came two days after researchers revealed eMudhra had issued eight certificates with private keys so defective they were trivial to discover. articles.title: Ryzen 5800X3D Revival was Lisa Su's Initiative, and Other Interesting Details in AMD Interview with MyNavi Tech+
articles.summary:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Ryzen 5800X3D Revival was Lisa Su's Initiative, and Other Interesting Details in AMD Interview with MyNavi Tech+
Japanese tech publication MyNavi Tech+ interviewed Travis Kirsch, the client-segment product manager for AMD, and there are some interesting excerpts from the conversation. It turns out that reviving Ryzen 7 5800X3D for the Socket AM4 market earlier this year, was an initiative going as far up as CEO Lisa Su. articles.title: 1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents log in without ever seeing the password - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents log in without ever seeing the password
Identity security company 1Password today launched 1Password for Agents, its new sign-in platform for personal artificial intelligence agents.
Agents from Meta Platforms Inc., Anthropic PBC, OpenAI Group PBC and Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI will be able to log in to people’s accounts through it without ever seeing the password.
1Password for Agents is aimed at a habit that took hold once agents started paying bills and planning vacations for people. Most of those jobs mean getting into an account. The easy route has been to paste the password into the agent’s chat window, which leaves a copy saved somewhere outside the owner’s control.
Aashish Tripathi, chief product officer at 1Password, said agents are “starting to do real work on our behalf.” In his view, an agent asked to do one task has no reason to walk away with permanent access to the whole account.
Under the new setup, the password never travels to the agent at all. A unique digital key identifies the agent to 1Password when it hits a login page, and the request that follows tells the person which account is wanted and for what. articles.title: Beyond The EPE Budget: Building The Next Generation Of Computational Lithography
articles.summary:
Why better models, richer metrology, explainable AI, and cross-industry collaboration must come together to extend semiconductor scaling.
At the recent SPIE Photomask Technology + Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography conference, an expert panel discussed the growing importance of edge placement error (EPE). I had the pleasure of joining moderator Jed Rankin of IBM and fellow panelists Hans Stiepan of Carl Zeiss SMT, Ezequiel Vidal-Russell of Micron Technology, Jo Finders of ASML, Il-Yong Jang of Tekscend, and Vivek Balasubramanian of Applied Materials. Together, we brought perspectives spanning OPC and EDA, mask technology, lithography systems, materials, and metrology. One point quickly became clear: EPE is no longer a narrow lithography metric. It is becoming a system-level measure of how well our industry can translate design intent into a manufacturable, high-yielding device. The mask, scanner, resist, etch process, metrology, OPC, and downstream integration all contribute. Each discipline can optimize its own part, but a collection of local optima does not automatically produce the best device—even if everyone arrives with an excellent slide explaining why their part is already optimized.

La Firefly a réussi à faire rentrer une batterie de 60 kWh dans une voiture dont l’empattement mesure 2,615 mètres. Ce nouveau pack batterie conserve exactement le même format extérieur et le même poids sur la balance que la batterie initiale de 42,1 kWh. Le secret tient à la chimie des cellules.

articles.title: CON, PRN und NUL: Warum du Dateien in Windows 11 nicht so benennen darfst
articles.summary:
Windows 11: Diese Dateinamen sind verboten – und der Grund stammt aus dem Jahr 1981
Obwohl Windows 11 ein modernes Betriebssystem ist und Microsoft darauf bedacht ist, viele Neuerungen zu implementieren, gibt es darin noch Relikte fast vergessener Zeiten. Dazu zählt etwa ein Feature, das nur wegen eines Kultspiels in Windows eingefügt wurde. Daneben gibt es aber auch alte Regeln, die Windows-User:innen heute noch einen Strich durch die Rechnung, oder besser gesagt die Dateibenennung, machen können.
Warum Windows 11 manche Dateinamen verbietet
Wie Windows Latest berichtet, gibt es eine Reihe von Namen und Kürzeln, die nicht für Dateien in Windows 11 genutzt werden dürfen. Versuchen es User:innen doch, verweigert das Betriebssystem die Eingabe und drängt darauf, einen anderen Namen für die Datei oder den Ordner zu wählen. Ai2 releases OlmoEarth v1.3 state-of-the-art AI-ready satellite embeddings for the whole planet
Ai2, the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, today released a satellite map embedding model called OlmoEarth v1.3 and precomputed annual embeddings for the whole planet at various resolutions with a browser-based map-making tool.
The model compresses a year of satellite observations into a numerical fingerprint for each 10-by-10-meter patch of ground at the smallest resolution, with 64-square-meter and 128-meter also available. That fingerprint captures patterns that other software can use to distinguish crops, forests, mines and other types of land cover.
Until now, the primary way to use OlmoEarth was to fine-tune in OlmoEarth Studio, train a model for each task and run it over satellite data to make a map. That requires access to vast graphics processing unit resources and the ability to download and store imagery.
With today’s launch, users can use OlmoEarth Embeddings Explorer, a browser-based map-making tool. That means anyone can turn OlmoEarth into real work, from tracking change over time to finding similar places – no sign-in required.
An embedding represents what a model learned from millions of satellite images. OlmoEarth reads a year of radar images from data, including Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Landsat. articles.title: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.

NASA does not have, nor want, nuclear weapons. But when it comes to a particular metric that is part of the Artemis Program to land people on the Moon, NASA guards a particular number like they are trying to prevent outsiders from cracking nuclear codes.
I am speaking of the number of Starship launches required to fuel a Starship-based lunar lander in low-Earth orbit such that it can fly out to the Moon, land there, and return to lunar orbit.
This number has been a moving target over the years. The general response from NASA has typically been, ‘We don’t know for sure, so we’re not going to say.’ In 2023, for example, the then-director of NASA’s Human Landing System, Lisa Watson-Morgan, told Ars, “We have a general idea, but I’m reluctant to say exactly what that is.”
Later, she said the number was in the “high single digits to the low double digits.” That suggests about a dozen launches, which is a lot. SpaceX would need to launch a “depot” Starship, and then 11 “tanker” Starships to fully load it with liquid oxygen and methane propellant for a lunar voyage. Other officials have said “high teens.” The hope has always been that SpaceX would dramatically improve the lift capacity of Starship to bring down the number of tanker flights.

articles.title: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
AI agents left to explore a virtual island without a specific task began inventing challenges of their own. MIT researchers say the behavior bears the hallmarks of play.
The researchers put 13 AI agents called Eko, each running on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. They describe the experiment in a paper posted on arXiv, a site where researchers share studies before peer review. Afterward, they gave the agents specific challenges, like getting as many objects as possible onto the island’s tallest rock spire. The Eko agents that had spent those 30 hours playing generally beat identical agents that had never set foot on the island.
Today, developers decide in advance what AI should practice and what counts as success. The researchers see this technique — exploring without a goal — as a different way for AI agents to learn skills, especially skills that could one day be used to control robots.
“We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress,” the researchers write in their report. “Play suggests another regime: give an agent a sufficiently rich and safe world, let it choose what is interesting, and allow useful knowledge to accumulate from the history that follows.”

articles.title: El miedo a la IA nace de nuestra incapacidad para entender cómo funciona. Un científico cree estar a punto de resolverlo

Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, Leo Gao, Stephen Wolfram y Dario Amodei tienen al menos dos cosas en común. Todos ellos, junto a muchos otros científicos, han contribuido a que la inteligencia artificial (IA) alcance el grado de desarrollo que tiene actualmente. Y, además, todos han reconocido abiertamente que no comprenden por completo cómo los modelos de lenguaje organizan y utilizan internamente lo que han aprendido durante su entrenamiento. De alguna forma, se comportan como cajas negras cuyo contenido es relativamente inaccesible.
"Personalmente, no creo que lleguemos a interpretar nunca lo que sucede dentro de las redes neuronales por razones fundamentales, aunque podemos obtener algunas pistas interesantes. Mi esperanza reside más bien en conseguir que el proceso por el que la IA llega a sus respuestas pueda descomponerse en partes interpretables". Yoshua Bengio pronunció estas palabras durante una charla organizada por el Instituto para el Futuro de la Vida, en octubre de 2024. Geoffrey Hinton fue más breve en una entrevista con Wired de 2019: "No, realmente no sabemos cómo funcionan".
Ya han pasado varios años desde que estos dos científicos hicieron estas declaraciones, pero en fechas mucho más recientes Sam Altman, Dario Amodei y otras personas relevantes de la industria de la IA han confesado que existen limitaciones a la hora de comprender el funcionamiento interno de los grandes modelos de lenguaje. Every year, thousands of families in Bihar move from one place to another in search of employment. A significant number of these families work at brick kilns. For them, migration is not simply about changing locations. It means changing homes and workplaces. In the process, children’s education often takes a back seat.
When a family leaves its village for a few months to work at a brick kiln, its children usually move with it. Schools may be located far away, and a lack of essential documents can make it difficult to access government services. Limited awareness of welfare schemes adds to the challenges. The impact is felt not only in children’s education but also in the entire family’s access to social security.
Anshu Kumar Jaiswal from Bihar had not encountered this challenge for the first time through a report or a set of statistics. He had witnessed it on the ground.
Between 2019 and 2021, while working with the Piramal Foundation as a Gandhi Fellow, he arrived in Sheikhpura. It was here that he came face to face with the lives of families living and working at brick kilns.

Ontario will make over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids available in the province for people with mild hearing loss. The province plans to make the legislative change in the fall economic update later this year, enabling these devices for use in the province.
The move should open up access to more affordable hearing aid options, as well as to solutions that use wireless earbuds as hearing aids — for example, Apple’s AirPods Pro (though it’s not yet clear when Apple will make the feature available to Ontarians).
Health Minister Sylvia Jones says that the change will give more Ontarians the flexibility to get the support they need.
Health Canada has previously given medical device licences for wireless earbuds with built-in hearing aid capabilities. However, provincial laws have so far prevented this, only allowing for hearing aids prescribed by a doctor or audiologist. The change will allow earbuds with built-in hearing aid capabilities to turn on this feature.
The Ontario government says this update will not replace or impact existing hearing aid prescriptions and coverage.
In June, B.C. allowed adults 18 years and older with mild to moderate hearing loss to purchase OTC hearing aids without a prescription.

Autonomy and control are not opposites, they go together: EY GDS at DevSparks Chennai
At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman of EY GDS made the case that moving agents into production is an engineering problem, not a model problem.
Ask a room of developers about agents today and you will get plenty of answers. Almost everyone has built one, and most have a demo they are proud of.
The harder question is what happens after that, when the agent has to hold up against real customers, real data, and real consequences. At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman, Global Cloud Consulting, Microsoft Practice and Alliances Leader at EY GDS, opened with a version of it. He asked how many people in the room had built an AI agent, and plenty of hands went up. Then he asked how many had built one that made it to production for a business-critical system. "I think that's where the numbers dramatically drop," he said. "Not because of anybody's fault, but that's how it is."
That gap is the whole problem, and it is not a model problem. Cloud, low code tools, and open model APIs have pushed the entry barrier close to zero. What has not changed is the difficulty of industrializing what you build. "Access to intelligence is not the bottleneck, but the ability to industrialize is going to be the bottleneck," said Arvind Purushothaman.

articles.title: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
articles.summary:
A security researcher has demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, gaining “userland” access that he says “lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO.”
The hack relies on the original Switch version of SmileBasic 4, the latest in a long-running series of programming environments and interpreters that run on Nintendo hardware. The so-called “tethered” hack also requires access to a macOS or Linux PC on the same network to run a node.js package that helps enable privileged system access.
Researcher Sammy Hajhamid writes that he used OpenAI’s Codex to poke at SmileBasic’s language interpreter, using a custom harness that could send USB commands to the system and view results via HDMI (as well as power cycling via a Bluetooth light switch flipping device). After “substantial effort for ~2 weeks,” that harness discovered a 32-bit integer overflow that occurs when removing items from an array in SmileBasic. That error gives access to an array pointer, which in turn allows read and write access to portions of system memory.
From there, Hajhamid writes that he started poking around for access to the Switch 2’s internal sysmodules, looking for ones that could provide more privileged access to the console’s core functions. Now, the Japanese designer is weighing in on the generative AI debate, arguing that LLM-based "stochastic parrots" don't have what it takes to create a truly original game IP.
In a recent interview with Japanese website Denfaminicogamer, Sakurai shared his well-informed opinions on how generative AI is going to impact the video game business. Developing new game "products" is becoming easier than ever, he said, but turning AI-generated slop into a profitable venture will take a lot more than a few chatbot prompts.
Sakurai explained that modern game designs usually stem from direct comparison with what's already on the market. That gives developers and publishers an easy way to show customers what they're getting for their money.

En se faisant passer pour le client, l’agent IA se connecte alors au compte, ce qui viole les règles de la plupart des banques. Certaines IA ont contacté les centres d’appels de la banque et ont pris « des initiatives indépendamment des instructions de l’utilisateur ». Betroffen war dabei das sogenannte Misalignment-Monitoring – eine Kontrollfunktion, die prüfen soll, ob Agenten sich an ihre Anweisungen halten – und die bei Auffälligkeiten Meldungen an das Entwicklerteam schickt. OpenAI untersucht nach eigenen Angaben noch, ob die Agenten übereifrig waren und/oder Anweisungen falsch verstehen – oder ob sie die Warnungen bewusst deaktiviert haben.
Ein Agent verschafft sich mehr Spielraum
Im ersten Fall sollte ein Agent mit dem Modell GPT-6 Astra Programmcode in eine Referenzumgebung übertragen. Das ist eine Testumgebung, in der sich beobachten lässt, was mit dem Code eines Nutzers passiert. Laut OpenAI-Bericht gab Astra die Aufgabe an einen Subagenten weiter – also an ein untergeordnetes System, das Teilaufgaben übernimmt.
In der Aufgabenstellung erwähnte Astra nicht, dass die Überwachung aktiv bleiben muss. Stattdessen trug es dem Subagenten nur auf, ein für die exakte Migration „angemessenes“ Framework umzusetzen. Der Subagent las das als Erlaubnis – oder sogar als Aufforderung, die Monitoring-Einstellungen der Referenzumgebung zu übernehmen statt der eigenen. Notably, the report found that 86 per cent of teens globally use AI for school, and Canadian teens who use AI every week for school scored two years behind those who never use it. Dubé adds that scores have overall been declining for years, coinciding with the 2022 release of ChatGPT, although he stresses that this in itself isn’t evidence of causality.
Instead, he looked further into how and why Canadian students are turning to AI. Here were some of the biggest use cases:
- “To help me learn” (38 per cent in Canada, 46 per cent globally)

articles.title: Nvidia driver update should greatly speed up PC games
articles.summary:
Nvidia has rolled out a new GPU driver that should significantly speed up game launches.
The update, 621.01, adds Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery tech to reduce the load on CPUs by offloading the heavy lifting to the cloud. As Nvidia notes, modern games rely on tens of thousands of complex shaders as well as generic shader files that result in a slow, CPU-heavy process that can take up to 30 minutes.
But with Microsoft’s latest tech, the cloud network can greatly cut down these wait times by precompiling shaders for hundreds of thousands of hardware and driver combinations. It also removes mid-game “just-in-time” shader compilation that can cause CPU spikes and frame stutters.
For now, this week’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and the recently released Gears of War: E-Day from Vancouver’s The Coalition support Advanced Shader Delivery. You’ll need to download these games via the Xbox PC app, but from there, you’ll benefit from the new shader system even when playing Steam games as long as the Xbox app remains installed.
The 621.01 update can be downloaded here. The new GPU driver comes as part of a larger series of updates to improve gaming on Nvidia GeForce. The full breakdown can be found on Nvidia’s blog.

Fibras de carbono, mucho más delgadas que un cabello humano, permiten esta captura con un consumo eléctrico bajo y una generación mínima de ozono. Durante la marcha, el propio flujo de aire generado por el movimiento del vehículo empuja el aire a través del sistema, lo que evita la necesidad de un soplador de alta potencia independiente.

articles.title: California exige revisión humana obligatoria antes de cualquier despido por IA a partir de 2027

California se convirtió en el primer estado de Estados Unidos en exigir que un humano confirme cualquier despido o sanción decidida por un sistema de inteligencia artificial. El gobernador Gavin Newsom firmó el 30 de septiembre la ley SB 947, que entrará en vigor el 1 de julio de 2027.
Conocida como No Robo Bosses Act, la norma prohíbe a los empleadores basarse exclusivamente en un sistema automatizado para despedir o disciplinar a un trabajador. Cuando lo usan como fuente principal de esa decisión, deben designar a un revisor humano que corrobore el resultado.
Ese revisor debe apoyarse en evaluaciones de jefes, archivos del legajo, revisiones de pares o el historial de trabajo del empleado. La empresa, además, debe notificar por escrito que la IA fue la herramienta principal de la decisión y describir los datos que usó.
La notificación también debe incluir el contacto de una persona que pueda explicar el resultado. El incumplimiento se castiga con una multa civil de USD 500 por infracción, exigible por la Comisión Laboral de California y por fiscales estatales y locales.
“Ningún trabajador debería ser despedido o sancionado por una máquina, sea o no inteligencia artificial”, dijo a CNBC el senador estatal Jerry McNerney, autor del proyecto. “La inteligencia artificial debe seguir siendo una herramienta controlada por humanos, y no al revés”, agregó el legislador demócrata.

Sous le plancher d’une voiture électrique, des dizaines de cellules travaillent en équipe. Il suffit que quelques-unes s’essoufflent plus vite pour que toute la batterie arrive en fin de vie, alors que les autres ont encore de la réserve. En épluchant les données de 116 voitures et 17 bus, des chercheurs ont mesuré l’ampleur du phénomène : près de 18 % de durée de vie en moins, et un seuil kilométrique au-delà duquel tout s’accélère.
Une batterie de voiture électrique assemble des dizaines, voire des milliers de cellules, censées vieillir au même rythme. Sur la route, elles divergent. Des chercheurs de l'Institut de physique chimique de Dalian (Académie chinoise des sciences), de l'université Chalmers en Suède, de l'Institut de technologie de Pékin et de la filiale européenne de Zeekr, marque premium du groupe Geely, ont épluché plus de trois ans de données issues de 116 voitures et 17 bus circulant en Chine.

In Nexus, historian and author Yuval Noah Harari examines how information networks have shaped human history and how they may influence our future. Published in 2024, the book explores the relationship between information, power, truth and the development of artificial intelligence.
Harari challenges the assumption that having more information automatically makes societies wiser or better informed.
What matters is how information is organised, who controls it and whether the systems that distribute it help people correct their mistakes. Here are five important lessons to learn from Nexus and how they apply to the world we live in today.

The company reports no sign the flaw has been used in attacks, and it is not listed in the U.S. CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities as of October 22.

La agencia ejerció así, por primera vez, un poder que había adoptado apenas unos días antes.
Según informó la FCC el 22 de octubre, los productos bloqueados son una cámara para autos y un transmisor inalámbrico de video. Ninguno de los dos había recibido todavía la autorización que la agencia exige para venderse en el país, y ambos quedaron frenados antes de completar ese trámite.

HiSilicon es la unidad de diseño de semiconductores de Huawei, incluida en la llamada Covered List, el listado de empresas que Washington considera una amenaza a la seguridad nacional desde marzo de 2021.
El presidente de la FCC, Brendan Carr, calificó a los aparatos de video que incorporan ese tipo de chips como “un riesgo obvio e inaceptable para la nación y su gente”. La agencia no identificó al fabricante ni el modelo exacto de los dos productos bloqueados.

After unauthorized access to the multi-tenant application, the group attempted sign-ins at more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, with stolen ConnectWise app credentials that authenticated as the apps with no interactive user sign-in. Some of the group’s attacks reached privileged access less than three hours after initial targeting.

Capcom a repéré l’intrusion le 19 octobre et l’a signalée deux jours plus tard à la police d’Osaka. Au total, 11 774 247 enregistrements sont concernés dans le monde, d’après le communiqué publié par l’éditeur. Capcom n’a trouvé aucune trace d’une fuite des mots de passe choisis par les joueurs, mais l’intrus a modifié celui de 196 comptes, et l’éditeur n’explique pas comment. articles.title: Two Dollars and a Test Suite - EE Times

The Arm-Qualcomm verdict made headlines for its $2 award. The finding that matters more is about who controls the compliance tests a custom chip must pass before it can ship.
The verdict nobody read closely
On Oct. 13, a federal jury in Delaware delivered the second verdict in two years between Arm and Qualcomm. The number that drew the most attention was the damages award: $2, one for each claim Qualcomm won. Both companies declared victory, and IMHO both had some reason to. Arm prevailed on four of the six claims. On the other hand, Qualcomm won a finding that Arm interfered with its business with Meta, plus an additional finding under its Architecture License Agreement that I think deserves far more attention than it received.
The jury found that Arm breached Qualcomm’s Architecture License Agreement by withholding two deliverables, ACKs and OOBs. To most people, these acronyms mean very little, which may explain why most coverage moved quickly on to royalties and to the $2. But they describe something we may know very well: the tests a custom processor must pass before anyone can call it an Arm processor.
What a compliance kit actually does
Arm licenses its technology in two ways. Most customers take Arm-designed cores “as is” and integrate them into their chips, under a Technology License Agreement (TLA). articles.title: New QPACK Flaws Can Crash HTTP/3 Servers, Trigger Up to 4,000-Fold Memory Amplification
articles.summary:
A remote attacker who has not logged in can crash many HTTP/3 web servers with a single connection, security firm FoxIO disclosed, releasing working proof-of-concept code.
By sending a small batch of compressed HTTP headers that expands in memory to a much larger set, the attacker can force the server to use thousands of times more memory than it received, enough to run a default server out of memory.
The flaws cause only denial-of-service attacks, with no evidence of data theft or code execution and no public reports of attacks in the wild. Fixes are out for quic-go, Cloudflare quiche, lsquic and Wireshark, but Bun, the h3 Rust library and aioquic were still unpatched at disclosure.
FoxIO found the same class of flaw in seven of ten HTTP/3 stacks it tested. The common cause is in QPACK, the scheme HTTP/3 uses to compress request headers so repeated fields travel as a short code instead of the full text.
A server is supposed to cap the size of the headers after it unpacks them. The affected stacks cap the compressed batch that arrives on the wire, but not the unpacked result, or they apply the cap too late, so a single request can expand into hundreds of thousands of header entries that the server holds in memory.
The reach is wide because these stacks sit under common software. quic-go is the Go library behind Caddy, Traefik and cloudflared; lsquic is LiteSpeed's library, used in LiteSpeed Web Server and OpenLiteSpeed; and Bun's HTTP/3 server runs on lsquic.

articles.title: Node.js Brotli Decoder Bug Could Allow Remote Code Execution in All Supported Versions
articles.summary:
Node.js released security updates on October 21 for its three supported release lines, 22.x, 24.x and 26.x, fixing 10 flaws. The most serious is a bug in the Brotli decompression code that Node.js bundles, which the project says can allow remote code execution, meaning an attacker could run code of their choosing on the affected system.
Each supported line has one fixed version: 22.23.4 and 24.22.1 on the long-term support lines, and 26.12.1 on the current line. Node.js 20.x and earlier have reached end of life and will not receive the fix, so they should be moved to a supported line.
The Brotli flaw is in code Node.js bundles, not in a user's own program. Node.js runs that code whenever it decompresses Brotli data, either directly through the node:zlib module or automatically when code calls fetch() on a response sent with Brotli compression.
An application is exposed where it decompresses Brotli data an attacker controls, such as a request body or a response fetched from another server.
The Brotli Flaw
The flaw is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder, set off by malformed compressed input. The fix is an upstream patch from the Brotli project that Node.js copied in, and it makes the decoder catch invalid input and stop earlier rather than writing past the buffer.
Brotli is Google's compression library, and Node.js ships its own copy. The same fix shipped in Brotli 1.2.1, 1.1.1, and 1.0.10 on October 21, so other software that bundles Brotli may need the same update. …

Google LLC’s cloud unit today introduced Agent Compute Engine, an infrastructure service optimized to host artificial intelligence agents.
AI agents run in technology environments called sandboxes. They host the applications, data and user instructions that agents need to carry out their work. Sandboxes also contain cybersecurity guardrails that block malicious activity.
Google refers to Agent Compute Engine’s implementation of sandboxes as microVMs. The company says that the technology combines the hardware efficiency of containers with the security of traditional virtualization. In particular, Google brought over hypervisors’ ability to isolate virtual machines from one another to prevent the spread of malware.
The company runs microVMs on specially configured appliances. The appliances are stateless, which means that they don’t permanently retain the files used by customers’ agents. The data that the systems do store is kept in an immutable file system that can’t be modified or deleted.
Google verifies the integrity of the appliances’ firmware using its custom Titan cybersecurity chips. The appliances’ central processing units, in turn, feature mitigations against side-channel attacks. Those are cyberattacks that analyze data about a CPU’s physical state to glean the customer information it processes.

articles.title: Oups, ce bug sur Signal permettait d'écouter la conversation même après avoir raccroché

Une faille critique corrigée dans la bibliothèque d’appels de Signal permettait à un correspondant de continuer à capter votre audio après que vous aviez raccroché. Le correctif existe depuis début septembre, mais la vulnérabilité vient seulement d’être rendue publique.
La faille, référencée CVE-2026-113380, touche toutes les versions de RingRTC antérieures à 2.72.0. Elle affiche un score de 9,3 sur 10 sur l’échelle de sévérité CVSS.
Une faille corrigée qui donne quelques sueurs froides
RingRTC est la bibliothèque open source derrière les appels vocaux et vidéo de Signal, sur mobile comme sur ordinateur. La faille ne touche pas le chiffrement des conversations. Elle concerne uniquement la façon dont un appel se termine. Aucun message, mot de passe ou historique n’a été exposé, et changer ses identifiants ne sert à rien ici.
Pour fonctionner, RingRTC s’appuie sur des machines à états. C’est un composant logiciel qui suit chaque étape d’un appel, et chaque action passe par une file d’événements. Y compris quand on raccroche et termine l’appel. Un appelant malveillant peut saturer cette file avec des requêtes. La demande de fin d’appel envoyée par votre téléphone n’est alors jamais traitée. L’appel paraît terminé à l’écran, mais votre micro continue d’émettre vers votre correspondant. Il devient alors possible d’entendre une remarque lâchée après avoir terminé l’appel, une discussion avec quelqu’un à côté ou du simple bruit de fond. Le descriptif de la vulnérabilité évoque aussi…

The working chain instead starts with a 32-bit integer overflow in SmileBASIC 4, a roughly $25 Switch 1 programming app that still runs on the Switch 2, and then moves to a buffer overflow in the console's filesystem service.
The end result lets users run native code with the permissions of ordinary system modules, which opens the door to homebrew, game mods, save backups, and reverse engineering. However, the jailbreak is tethered, so it has to be run again after every reboot, and there's no kernel exploit or custom firmware yet. Esa anticipación de compras dejó al tercer trimestre con poca demanda real para sostener el ritmo habitual de ventas. El sueño bifásico es un patrón de sueño en el que las horas de sueño se reparten en dos bloques separados por un periodo de vigilia. Se trata de un patrón de sueño popularizado por el historiador Roger Ekirch y por el psiquiatra Thomas Wehr que de manera independiente estudiaron el fenómeno.

Esto lo llevó a compilar una serie de pruebas historiográficas, procedentes tanto de la ficción como de documentos oficiales, de la existencia de un sueño bifásico en estos periodos.

Tras este hiato del sueño, nuestros antepasados habrían vuelto a dormir, esta vez hasta el amanecer.

articles.title: OpenCode Flaw Lets Malicious MCP Servers Execute Code During Sign-In on Windows and WSL
articles.summary:
A flaw in the OpenCode AI coding agent allowed a malicious or hijacked MCP server to run code on a developer's Windows or WSL machine when the developer signed in. OpenCode connects to MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to add outside tools, and such code would run with the developer's own access.
Anomaly, the company behind OpenCode, fixed the flaw in version 1.18.33 on September 28. It did not request a CVE or publish a security advisory, so vulnerability scanners will not flag the builds still at risk: 1.0.137 through 1.18.32.
During that sign-in, the server itself supplies the web address the user is sent to, an OAuth "authorization endpoint." On Windows and WSL, OpenCode handed that address to a helper that opens it in a browser. The helper built a PowerShell command around the address without escaping it, so an address written to carry a PowerShell command would run that command.
The browser step runs only when a developer starts the sign-in, by running opencode mcp auth or making the matching request. Having the server configured, or opening a session, does not reach it.
The attacker needs control of a remote MCP server the developer has added, and that server need not be hostile from the start. One that is later taken over, or a domain that changes hands, could carry the same address.
Pillar Security, which found the flaw and disclosed it on October 19, rates it critical, with a proposed severity score of 9.8 out of 10.

LLMs are roughly divided into two categories: closed commercial efforts from frontier labs, whose models are expensive to run but deliver excellent results, and Chinese open-weight competitors that broadly exchange reliability for a much cheaper running cost, particularly for long-running agentic tasks.

articles.title: Railway Says Intruder May Have Accessed Customer Secrets, Urges Credential Rotation
articles.summary:
Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) provider Railway on Wednesday disclosed "anomalous activity" related to systems that store customer environment variables.
Upon further investigation, the company found that an unauthorized third party may have gained access to encrypted environment variables, and, in some cases, obtained the decrypted contents. The impact, it said, is limited to a "subset of users," although it did not disclose an exact number.
Environment variables refer to user-defined key-value pairs that are used to store sensitive data like API keys, database credentials, or feature flags. They are configured at the operating system or container environment level instead of hard-coding the values directly into a program's source code.
Railway said the incident is likely part of a series of attacks designed to target platform companies with the ultimate goal of compromising artificial intelligence (AI) inference providers. The company also said it has notified upstream providers to proactively revoke the keys so as to prevent their abuse.
Customers are being urged to take the following actions as a precautionary measure -
- Rotate environment variables, including any API keys, stored in Railway, as well as private registry credentials.
- Review logs for those services for unusual activity
