articles.title: You thought your ChatGPT conversations were private. The courts disagree.
articles.summary:
You thought your ChatGPT conversations were private. The courts disagree.
A growing number of cases show your LLM chats are anything but private
Do you remember those 200 questions you asked ChatGPT — the ones you’d be far too embarrassed to ask your own mom?
You may have thought it was all confidential, but a growing number of cases show these chats are not protected by any legal safeguards and could end up in court.
In May 2025, a US court ordered OpenAI to hand over more than 20 million ChatGPT logs that users had previously deleted in connection with the New York Times copyright case.
And just two months ago, a Washington Post investigation revealed that at least a dozen court cases had cited logs from AI chatbots as evidence, highlighting that users’ most intimate confessions could be used for legal purposes.
In US v. Heppner, Judge Jed Rakoff ruled that a defendant's Claude conversations weren't shielded by attorney-client privilege or work-product protection, reasoning that no attorney-client relationship exists "or could exist, between an AI user and a platform such as Claude."
"Most people treat an AI like a private diary. But legally, it’s a record held by a company, with none of the privilege that protects what you tell a lawyer or a doctor," Eamonn Maguire, Director of Engineering and Machine Learning at Proton — which develops its own privacy-focused AI assistant — tells TechRadar.
Despite this, people continue to ignore the weight that their digital diaries carr…

According to multiple reports from the Associated Press, the New York Times, Reuters, and the Wall Street Journal, state District Court Judge Francis J. Mathew called out Meta and Facebook for making misleading statements about the privacy of consumers in the state.
"Facebook promised users that they (the users) controlled their data," Mathew wrote in his ruling. "This was false."
The penalty relates to more than 43 million violations of the state's unfair practices law. articles.title: Goldman Sachs prevé que la IA desplace a uno de cada once trabajadores en Estados Unidos
articles.summary:
El economista jefe de Goldman Sachs, Joseph Briggs, estimó que la inteligencia artificial podría desplazar hasta al 9% de los trabajadores de Estados Unidos durante la próxima década, una cifra equivalente a uno de cada once empleados del país.
La proyección aparece en una nota publicada el 22 de octubre por Briggs, economista global del banco, y fue adelantada por la revista Fortune. El 9% equivale a 15 millones de trabajadores que perderían su puesto a lo largo de lo que Goldman llama la “transición de la IA”.
Pero el hallazgo central de la nota no es el número, sino el momento en que ocurrirá. Según Briggs, “la disrupción laboral vinculada a la automatización es limitada cuando la economía está sana, pero se acelera durante las desaceleraciones cíclicas”.
Es decir, mientras el empleo y el crecimiento se mantengan firmes, las empresas tendrán menos incentivos para reemplazar personal con IA. El verdadero recorte de puestos llegaría recién cuando se desate una recesión, sostiene el economista.
“Las disrupciones laborales vinculadas a la IA podrían amplificar el ciclo económico general”, escribió Briggs en la nota difundida el jueves.
Cómo pasó pronóstico del 6% al 9%
La cifra no salió de la nada. En agosto de 2025, Briggs y la economista Sarah Dong habían calculado que la IA podría desplazar entre el 6% y el 7% de la fuerza laboral estadounidense, dentro de un rango posible de entre el 3% y el 14%.

A day after EA shut down BioWare, a trailer for the canceled next Mass Effect game has leaked online, and it seems the game was going to be called Mass Effect: Universe. Reddit user Random_Hyabusa_Ninja posted the roughly two-minute clip on r/masseffect on October 22, first in the replies of another post, and then as a standalone post. It follows a new human protagonist, with no sign of Shepard, through a tense bar conversation with an Asari who appears to be Liara T'Soni, cuts to a few gunfights and a Krogan, and ends on the Mass Effect: Universe logo.
The leak also raises questions about how far along the game actually was. EA's internal memo described it as being in early development, and around 50 of the 400 jobs EA is cutting were tied to it. However, a Reddit user claiming to be an EA employee said the trailer had been ready for months and that the project was further along than people think. BioWare first teased the game back in 2020, so that claim doesn't seem far-fetched, but its source is questionable at best. There's no word from EA on the leak so far, though it's reasonable to expect takedown requests to follow.

articles.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
articles.summary:
Linux servers running KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, are exposed to two publicly reported remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative, with no fix yet in the mainline kernel.
One of them, ZDI-CAN-33774, can be triggered before any network authentication. The other, ZDI-CAN-33549, requires the SMB Direct transport and an RDMA-capable network interface.
ZDI-CAN-33549 is an integer underflow in KSMBD's SMB Direct path. A client can supply RDMA buffer descriptors in which the first is longer than the declared payload, causing the server's size counter to wrap and allowing a subsequent memory copy to overrun the end of an allocated buffer.
It requires three things: an RDMA-capable interface (hardware or the rxe software driver), a writable KSMBD share, and a client negotiating SMB Direct.
ZDI-CAN-33774 requires no authentication, exposing any server running KSMBD on port 445. The flaw is a race in how KSMBD assigns its handler table: a burst of short SMB1 packets followed by an SMB2 packet in the same TCP write causes workers to handle SMB1 data with an SMB2 handler, reading past the end of the shorter buffer. A path to writing past the buffer also exists once an attacker has access to a share.
As of Thursday, neither flaw has a named fix in the mainline kernel or in linux-next, the integration tree that feeds it. Linux news site Phoronix said SMB Direct maintainer Stefan Metzmacher submitted a fix for ZDI-CAN-33549 targeting the next kerne…

Factores como la luz, la temperatura, la calidad del aire y el ruido de fondo forman parte de un conjunto de condiciones que puede facilitar el trabajo intelectual o, por el contrario, sumar pequeñas distracciones que terminan afectando el rendimiento frente a la pantalla.

La misma investigación identificó que las temperaturas interiores de entre 22 y 26 grados Celsius están vinculadas a mejores puntuaciones de creatividad. Estos hallazgos no apuntan a la existencia de una oficina perfecta, sino a que el pensamiento creativo también responde a condiciones físicas concretas que pueden medirse y ajustarse.
Por qué el aire y la temperatura condicionan el pensamiento creativo

articles.summary:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Micron Walks Away From 4F² DRAM After Two Decades of Research, Bets on 3D DRAM Instead
Micron has decided not to bring 4F² DRAM to market, even though it says it invented the cell design and has been researching it for around two decades. Scott DeBoer, Micron's President and Chief Technology and Products Officer, shared the decision during the company's technology webinar on October 21. On paper, 4F² uses vertical channel transistors to shrink each memory cell's footprint by about a third compared with the 6F² layout used in today's DRAM. However, DeBoer argued that real-world density is limited by how closely the capacitors can be packed, not by the cell's footprint, calling the density advantage over 6F² "a bit of a myth." He also said 4F² can be built, but at a higher cost and complexity, and that it runs into fundamental scaling problems at leading-edge nodes, which points toward 3D DRAM instead.
That puts Micron at odds with its rivals. Samsung and SK hynix are both developing 4F² designs, and China's CXMT says its first 4F² product will be a server DDR5 RDIMM due by the end of this year. Micron will keep scaling 6F² instead, with its 1-delta node set to ramp in Boise, Idaho, in the second half of 2027 and the 1-epsilon node after it moving to wafer bonding. 3D DRAM is being developed as a parallel path, but there's no timeline yet, and Micron says it will only switch once the economics make sense. eMudhra said it will replace affected customers' certificates with free ones from partners, though its announcement did not name the partners or provide a date for the exit.
Six of those eight were for website (TLS) certificates. Chrome will stop trusting the eMudhra root certificate above them, emSign ECC Root CA - G3. The change is expected to reach users on the morning of October 27, Pacific time.
On October 20, Mozilla decided to stop trusting the same root in Firefox. Removing a root from a browser also cuts off legitimate certificates issued beneath it.
About 30,800 unexpired certificates chained to that root as of October 21, by Chrome's count of public Certificate Transparency (CT) logs. Attackers are exploiting a zero-day SQL injection flaw in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, the company said in an advisory on October 22.
The flaw lets anyone who can log in to the orchestrator, even with a read-only customer account, gain operator privileges, the top level of control over it.
For on-premises orchestrators, the fix is in VCO 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12, while Hosted and Dedicated orchestrators have already been patched.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-114625 and rated 9.9 on the CVSS scale. Orchestrators running the releases that fixed the VCO flaws exploited in July and September are still affected, because those releases are older than the new fixes.
Arista bought the VeloCloud SD-WAN product line from Broadcom, announcing the deal in July 2025. The products were earlier known as VMware SD-WAN by VeloCloud.
To exploit the flaw, an attacker needs network access to the orchestrator's web interface and a valid login. The minimum role is Enterprise Read Only, the lowest built-in role for customer users. VCO is exposed by default, and no VCO setting prevents the exposure.
In VCO, operators create the customer and partner accounts, and each partner can manage a group of customers. The flaw allows an attacker to act as a local superuser, a role with full access. It may also allow an attacker to affect the VCO host itself and expose, modify, or disrupt the orchestrator and the data it manages.

articles.title: Your data is in Europe. Your technology still isn’t sovereign
articles.summary:
Your data is in Europe. Your technology still isn’t sovereign
Technical autonomy is harder than server geography - but much more important
On 12 June, thousands of organizations discovered an uncomfortable truth about the AI tools they had started building into their businesses. They didn’t have control over it.
The US government issued an export-control directive affecting two Anthropic models. Anthropic responded by disabling them for every customer. The restrictions were later lifted, but that is hardly reassuring. Access disappeared and then reappeared because of decisions customers neither made nor controlled.
Founder of Cycloid.
It’s a wake-up call that many claimed that they had after the Cloudflare outage… or the CrowdStrike outage… or Meta’s… or AWS’… or so on… And yet we were met with predictable surprise amongst an industry that has been so afraid of having potentially uncomfortable conversations around digital sovereignty.
We often talk about data-center locations, regional availability and compliance certificates. We discuss whether the server sits in York or New York, then congratulate ourselves for making a sovereign choice.
But if a foreign government can remove your service, an outage can take down your entire business, a vendor can change your operating model or a proprietary API makes migration economically impossible, the location of the server is almost beside the point.
Data residency is a comfort blanket

Según explicó, el Gobierno trabaja para recuperar el funcionamiento de las plataformas afectadas sin poner en riesgo la infraestructura digital pública.
La funcionaria subrayó que las interrupciones obedecen, en gran medida, a decisiones de precaución adoptadas mientras se aplican medidas de mitigación. El objetivo es restablecer los servicios de manera segura y evitar que las vulnerabilidades puedan ser aprovechadas por actores maliciosos.
Por su parte, una portavoz de Downing Street, la residencia oficial del primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, indicó que el incidente no ha comprometido los servicios públicos considerados críticos. Sin embargo, no detalló qué plataformas gubernamentales permanecen fuera de servicio ni cuánto tiempo podría tomar su recuperación.

articles.title: PHP2Shell Exploit Attempts Hit Millions as Attackers Try to Deploy Mirai Malware
articles.summary:
Threat actors have been observed unsuccessfully attempting to exploit the newly disclosed PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to rope infected systems into a Mirai botnet variant called Potassium, as it emerges that weaponizing the flaws may be harder than previously thought.
The attacks aim to exploit CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS scores: 9.2), which can result in unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) via specially crafted HTTP requests. The vulnerabilities have been patched in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.
"However, analysis of the sample revealed that it is an updated and significantly expanded version of the Mirai-derived botnet variant identified in early 2026," Sophos said. "The sample displays downloader and network disruption functionality."
Specifically, it resolves a hard-coded, encrypted command-and-control (C2) address, establishes a TCP connection to 134.199.154[.]64, and sends an HTTP request. The malware then checks for an HTTP 200 response status and verifies that the resulting payload begins with the ELF magic bytes 7F 45 4C 46, indicating that it expects a Linux ELF binary as a follow-on payload.
"A resolver function supports IPv4 addresses and hostname resolution, with additional fallback resolution logic that includes hard-coded public DNS servers such as 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, and 1.0.0.1," Sophos added. "As with Mirai malware historically, this sample can execute DDoS attacks."

articles.title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
articles.summary:
AI agents paying for API calls with the x402 SDKs could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it, security firm V12 said on October 22.
The cause was the SDKs' default client, which set no spending limit until releases on August 18 added one. The risk was limited to agents who automatically signed payments and whose apps set no limits.
The missing limit is one of 25 flaws V12 found in the x402 code, and one of three it rated critical and described in detail. The x402 Foundation, which maintains the SDKs, had already fixed all three critical flaws in the August 18 releases.
One of the other two let a facilitator, the service that checks x402 payments, accept a Solana transaction that moved no tokens as a valid payment. Among the x402 SDKs, only the TypeScript one had this flaw. The other let a malicious server get an agent to sign a login message for a different website.
V12 found the flaws by reviewing the code and running local tests. Neither V12 nor the x402 Foundation has publicly reported any attacks using them.
The foundation has published no security advisory for the three flaws, and its changelogs list the fixes without calling them security fixes. As of October 23, npm audit returned no advisories for the last TypeScript releases before the fixes, and PyPI listed no vulnerabilities for the last Python release before them, The Hacker News found. A developer who relies on those checks gets no warning to upgrade.

articles.title: ¿Es la IA una amenaza para el medio ambiente? Las cifras y su impacto en el consumo de energía, agua y minerales
articles.summary:
La expansión de la inteligencia artificial suele medirse por la rapidez con que genera textos, imágenes o videos, pero su funcionamiento depende de una infraestructura física que consume recursos. Detrás de cada respuesta hay centros de datos, edificios que concentran servidores y equipos de procesamiento y que requieren electricidad de forma constante.
Una parte de esa energía se transforma en calor. Para evitar el sobrecalentamiento, los centros de datos emplean sistemas de refrigeración, cuya función es retirar ese calor mediante aire, agua u otras tecnologías. Esta necesidad sumó inquietudes ambientales al crecimiento de la herramienta, debido a la demanda de electricidad, agua y materiales para fabricar y renovar el hardware.

articles.title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
articles.summary:
Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated.
Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or custom build, by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497). Node.js disclosed the flaw and released fixes on October 21, and applications that decode untrusted Brotli data should update.
Imperva's test did not succeed on every attempt, and code execution took several tries in its Linux arm64 setup. The result covers that one build and application setup, with other architectures and the 22.x and 26.x lines not tested. On the fixed release, 24.22.1, the same data was rejected, and no code ran.
The demonstration goes beyond the first public proof of concept, which achieved code execution only on a deliberately weakened test build. On a standard build, that proof of concept's author reported a crash and a limited read of process memory, not code execution, and said a working attack on a normal build was not achieved.
No exploitation of the flaw in the wild has been reported as of October 22.

articles.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
articles.summary:
Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open.
The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.
Ghostscript can read a name chosen by an attacker as instructions rather than as a file, and point it to a second file that carries commands to run. Pillow's maintainers fixed it in version 13.0.0, released on October 16.
Pillow turns up almost everywhere Python handles images: web upload forms, avatar and thumbnail tools, document and PDF pipelines, and most machine-learning projects pull it in. OX Security, the firm whose report drew attention to the flaws, estimates the library is downloaded about 436 million times a month.
Version 13.0.0 is a large security release, with fixes across four severity levels, from low to critical, two of which are rated critical by the maintainers. None of the flaws is known to be under attack.
The weakness is the filename, not the picture. "The flaw is triggered by the filename, not by anything in the PostScript document," the advisory says, meaning a harmless EPS file can still cause damage when an attacker sets its name. That makes upload endpoints that keep or build a stored file's name from user input the realistic target.

El modelo ya está disponible para todos los usuarios de Canva a nivel mundial desde la pestaña Dream Lab del menú de la aplicación, según informó la empresa en un comunicado publicado en su sala de prensa.
También puede usarse a través de la API pública de Canva, pensada para que desarrolladores integren la herramienta en plataformas de marketing, comercio electrónico o sitios de impresión.
Craft genera imágenes de hasta 2.000 píxeles de resolución en más de 30 proporciones de aspecto distintas. articles.title: PHP Warns of Another Unpatched RCE Two Days After Emergency PHP2Shell Patches
articles.summary:
PHP has warned of another way an attacker could run code on a web server, two days after it shipped emergency fixes for the critical PHP2Shell flaws.
The new issue, assigned CVE-2026-115560, affects only web applications configured in an unusual way, and PHP considers it an unlikely risk.
The project is not issuing an emergency fix for it. Instead, it recommends turning off a feature called session upload progress until a fix is available in the next routine release.
The warning came in a short informational advisory published on October 23. It follows the October 21 emergency release that fixed two critical PHP2Shell flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which let an attacker without an account run code on a server. Those were patched in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. The new issue is separate and is not fixed by those releases.
Only a narrow setup is at risk. PHP says the problem can occur when a web application does all of the following: sets the session.serialize_handler option to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration, then changes that option to php while running by calling ini_set(), and makes that change before it calls session_start().
Session upload progress must also still be turned on. An application that never changes the serialize handler while running can leave the feature on and is not exposed through this path. PHP says this setup is unlikely in practice.

It's still very early, but the developer says it already runs Minecraft: Xbox One Edition "extremely well," and the attached video shows it running on iOS with touchscreen controls. According to the project's GitHub page, Minecraft hits around 36 to 60 FPS on the Mac build, and Sonic Mania and Rocket League run there too, complete with screenshots. Sonic Mania is marked as playable at around 57 FPS with sound, while Rocket League renders and drives at roughly 15 to 20 FPS, with dark lighting and no audio yet.
Utsuro also works differently from a typical emulator. Apparently, it skips hardware emulation altogether and runs the console's Windows-based software layer as x86-64 code on Apple's Arm chips through FEXCore, and fills in the system pieces the console itself would normally provide. Graphics go through Apple's Metal API, with the Xbox One's Direct3D 11.X shaders converted to Metal's shader language, while audio runs on CoreAudio. Getting it running isn't exactly simple either. On iOS, the app has to be sideloaded, needs a JIT helper like StikDebug, TrollStore, or a jailbroken device, and expects a decrypted dump of the game. Spotify lanzó su primera aplicación nativa para autos, un software que corre directamente en la pantalla del vehículo sin necesidad de conectar un teléfono por cable o Bluetooth. La novedad llegó primero a varios modelos de Audi y busca reducir la dependencia de Apple CarPlay y Android Auto.
La nueva app se instala desde la tienda de aplicaciones del propio auto y funciona sobre Android Automotive, el sistema operativo de Google que corre directamente en el hardware del vehículo. Según dijo, el objetivo es ofrecer una experiencia que la empresa controle por completo, sin depender de las reglas de diseño de terceros.
“Estamos dibujando todos los píxeles”, dijo Tarlton. “No estamos dentro de una plantilla ni de un marco ajeno. Es 100% Spotify”, agregó el ejecutivo, en referencia a la versión anterior de la app para autos, que dependía de plantillas fijadas por Google.

articles.title: Authentication does not equal authorization: Are we asking passkeys to prove too much?
articles.summary:
Authentication does not equal authorization: Are we asking passkeys to prove too much?
A passkey confirms who logged in, not what they intended
By nearly all accounts, we’re inching closer to a passwordless society. The FIDO Alliance, which develops new passwordless authentication standards and whose tagline is quite literally “reducing reliance on passwords”, now estimates that more than 5 billion passkeys are in use worldwide. In fact, more than three-quarters of global consumers have already enabled a passkey on at least one account.
The technology is a boon for the financial industry because it finally removes the sector’s entrenched dependency on knowledge-based credentials – reusable “secrets” that criminals can steal, guess, or extract through social engineering. Suddenly, being able to quote a user’s mother’s maiden name, the town they grew up in, or their several-digit password, isn’t enough – and that makes user access instantly more secure.
Passkeys also give customers a much easier ride when it comes to accessing their accounts, speeding up the process by allowing them to use a key biometric like a fingerprint rather than hopping through two or three screens and entering their “memorable information” each time they log on.

YMTC to Start Mass Production of LPDDR5X with 9,600 MT/s Speed
YMTC, known as a NAND Flash manufacturer, is reportedly preparing to start mass production of LPDDR5X memory. While it has been known for some time that YMTC plans to enter DRAM production alongside its main NAND Flash business, it was not widely known that the company had already begun low-scale manufacturing. According to Counterpoint Research, YMTC has been producing about 5,000 wafers per month of 16 Gb LPDDR5X DRAM running at 7,500 MT/s at its Fab 2 since October 2025. The company is now preparing to begin volume production of LPDDR5X memory with speeds of 9,600 MT/s at its Fab 3, using Vertical Channel Transistor (VCT) 4F² cell structure technology.
YMTC has a significant advantage with 3D silicon, which represents the next phase of memory evolution. With its Xtacking 4.0 technology, YMTC can separate memory cell wafers from peripheral logic circuits and combine them using hybrid bonding wafer-to-wafer stacking. Hybrid bonding creates a permanent bond between two silicon chips using embedded metal bumps that are fused together to form a single chip. Multiple dies or entire silicon wafers can be connected by stacking the back ends of two chips together.Even if the company continues large-scale manufacturing of LPDDR5X, it can easily transition into 3D DRAM with its Xtacking 4.0 or possibly a future 5.0 iteration, which has yet to be seen. Scientists think they’ve calculated the exact night when Van Gogh painted The Starry Night — but not everyone agrees with the July 22, 1889 date
Finding the exact date of a masterpiece
- Scientists say they’ve dated Van Gogh’s The Starry Night
- Study says the painting was made on July 22, 1889
- The researchers used AI and CAD tools to help find an answer
The Starry Night by Vincent Van Gogh is one of the most famous paintings in the world, and it’s generally held that the artist finished the work in June 1889, shortly before a serious mental breakdown. But a new scientific study has attempted to see if technology can find the exact date that the masterpiece was made — and it’s come to a quite different conclusion to past experts.
Research published in the journal Scientific Reports argues that not only was the painting based on a real night sky rather than pulled from Van Gogh’s imagination, but that July 22, 1889 is the most likely candidate for the date of the composition. That flies in the face of the conventional wisdom, and not everyone is happy with that verdict.
The study’s authors reached that conclusion by first identifying the likely location where Van Gogh stood to paint the scene, concluding that he used a narrow field of view when selecting which stars to depict.
